front_matter.purpose:
## Purpose

This Policy & Procedure Manual sets out how **[AGENCY NAME]** ("the Agency") operates as a non-skilled personal care provider in the State of Florida. It is written to meet the requirements of Chapter 400, Part III, Florida Statutes, and Chapter 59A-8, Florida Administrative Code, as enforced by the Florida Agency for Health Care Administration (AHCA).

The manual is built for the Agency's chosen operating model. **[AGENCY NAME]** should confirm which one applies before adoption:

1. **Home Health Agency (HHA) license limited to non-skilled services.** The Agency provides hands-on personal care through home health aides and certified nursing assistants (CNAs), with registered nurse (RN) supervision. It does not provide skilled nursing.
2. **Homemaker and Companion Services registration (s. 400.509, F.S.).** The Agency provides companion and homemaker care only, with **no hands-on personal care**.
3. **Nurse Registry (s. 400.506, F.S.).** This is an alternative model in which referred caregivers are independent contractors and the registry may not supervise them. Use only the sections marked for the registry model.

The manual is intended to:

- Give the Agency's administrator, alternate administrator, supervising RN, office staff and caregivers one written, consistent set of rules for admission, service agreements, supervision, aide training, medication assistance, client records, emergency management, client rights and discontinuation of operations.
- Show AHCA surveyors, at the licensure survey and at unannounced surveys, that the Agency has the written policies and procedures the rules require.
- Protect clients by setting clear limits on what staff may and may not do. For example, companions and homemakers may not provide hands-on personal care, and unlicensed staff may assist with medication only within the limits of s. 400.488, F.S.
- Support the Agency's non-clinical compliance duties, including advertising, background screening, dementia training, wage-and-hour rules and workers' compensation.

This manual is a compliance tool. It does not replace the statutes and rules cited in it, and it is not legal advice. If the manual conflicts with current law, current law controls.

## How to Use This Manual

### Customize it before use
This manual is a template. Every place that shows **[AGENCY NAME]** or another bracketed placeholder must be replaced with the Agency's actual information before the manual is adopted or submitted. This includes the Agency name, license or registration number, address, counties served, administrator and alternate administrator, supervising RN, emergency coordinator and contact numbers. Delete or mark "not applicable" any section that does not fit the Agency's chosen model (HHA non-skilled license, homemaker/companion registration, or nurse registry). The Agency must not adopt policies it does not actually follow.

### Adopt it formally
The Agency's governing body (owner, board of directors or managing members) must review and formally adopt the manual. Record the adoption date, the signatures and the version number on the adoption page. Keep the signed adoption record with the manual.

### Keep it current
- Review the manual at least annually. The emergency management plan must also be reviewed annually (Rule 59A-8.027, F.A.C.).
- Revise it whenever a statute, rule or AHCA form changes, or when the Agency changes services, ownership, address, counties served or administrator.
- Record each revision with its date and the governing body's approval. Retire superseded versions but keep copies.
- Verify rule text against the official Florida Administrative Code on flrules.org. Unofficial copies, such as Cornell LII pages, may show an outdated version. For example, the 5/31/2026 version of Rule 59A-8.0095, F.A.C., controls.

### Train staff on it
All staff must be trained on the manual before they work with clients and again whenever it changes. Keep a signed acknowledgment, training date and trainer name for each person in the personnel file. This training is in addition to the training the law requires, such as aide training and competency, medication-assistance training, annual in-service, CPR, HIV/AIDS and dementia training. The Agency should keep a copy of the manual available to all staff and make it available to AHCA surveyors on request.

### Find what you need
- The manual is organized by operational topic (admission, service agreements, supervision, personnel, medication assistance, records, emergency management, and so on). Each policy identifies the rule or statute it implements.
- **Appendix A is the crosswalk to the official review items.** It maps every official item AHCA reviews to the policy in this manual that satisfies it. Use Appendix A to prepare for the survey, to confirm nothing is missing and to locate the right policy quickly during an unannounced survey.
- Sample forms (service agreement, client record, supervisory visit note, medication-assistance consent and record) are included as attachments. Adapt them to the Agency's operations.

## Regulatory Framework

### Governing statutes and rules
The rules below are cited exactly as they appear in the Agency's verified citation list. Staff should read the full official text, not just the summaries here.

**Licensure, registration and operations**

- **Ch. 400, Part III, F.S. (ss. 400.461-400.518)**: Home Health Services. This is the governing statute for HHAs and nurse registries. It covers licensure, staffing, service agreements, RN supervision and homemaker/companion registration.
- **s. 400.462, F.S.**: Definitions. Companions and homemakers may not provide hands-on personal care. Home health aides provide hands-on personal care.
- **s. 400.464, F.S.**: A license is required to provide hands-on care. The license number must appear in advertising. Advertising services not on the license is unlicensed activity.
- **s. 400.471, F.S.**: Application for license and fee. Includes CPA-compiled 2-year projections, proof of $250,000 per claim malpractice and liability insurance, and the licensure survey. Non-skilled agencies are exempt from accreditation.
- **s. 400.476, F.S.**: Staffing requirements and administrator qualifications. A director of nursing is required only for agencies providing skilled nursing.
- **s. 400.509, F.S.**: Registration of homemaker and companion providers. The registration number must appear in ads, and each worker's employment history must be verified.
- **s. 400.506, F.S.**: Licensure of nurse registries (nurse registry model only).
- **s. 408.810, F.S.**: Minimum licensure requirements. Includes reporting changes to AHCA, notice before discontinuing operation, client notices (complaint, abuse hotline and Medicaid fraud hotline), proof of legal right to occupy and the affidavit of compliance with s. 408.051(3).
- **s. 408.8065, F.S.**: Additional licensure requirements for home health agencies (startup, working-capital and contingency funds; surety bond where applicable).
- **Rule 59A-8.003, F.A.C.**: Licensure Requirements (application, surveys, change of ownership, satellite offices, change of address, public availability, surveyor access, RN supervisor availability policy, return of license on closure).
- **Rule 59A-8.008, F.A.C.**: Scope of Services.
- **Rule 59A-8.025, F.A.C.**: Registration Requirements for Homemaker and Companion Services Providers.

**Clients, services and records**

- **s. 400.487, F.S.**: Home health service agreements, plan of care, RN supervisory visits and DNR orders.
- **s. 400.488, F.S.**: Assistance with self-administration of medication and with other tasks.
- **Rule 59A-8.020, F.A.C.**: Acceptance of Patients or Clients.
- **Rule 59A-8.0215, F.A.C.**: Plan of Care.
- **Rule 59A-8.022, F.A.C.**: Clinical Records.
- **Rule 59A-8.027, F.A.C.**: Emergency Management Plans.

**Personnel, screening and training**

- **Rule 59A-8.0095, F.A.C.**: Personnel (administrator, RN supervision, aide training and competency, annual in-service, medication-assistance training, homemaker and companion duties).
- **s. 400.4785, F.S.**: Patients with Alzheimer's disease or other related disorders; staff training requirements; certain disclosures.
- **s. 430.5025, F.S.**: Dementia-related staff training.
- **s. 408.809, F.S.**: Background screening; prohibited offenses.
- **s. 435.12, F.S.**: Care Provider Background Screening Clearinghouse.

**Employment and payer requirements**

- **Fla. Const. Art. X, s. 24; s. 448.110, F.S.; s. 218.077, F.S.**: Florida minimum wage and preemption.
- **29 CFR 552.109**: Third party employment. An agency may not claim the FLSA companionship or live-in exemptions, so overtime applies.
- **s. 440.02, F.S.**: Workers' compensation definitions. Coverage is mandatory for a non-construction employer with four or more employees.
- **42 U.S.C. 1396b(l)**: Electronic visit verification for Medicaid personal care and home health services.
- **42 CFR 438.602**: State responsibilities (screening and enrollment of managed care network providers).
- **Rule 59G-4.002, F.A.C.**: Provider reimbursement schedules and billing codes.
- **iBudget Waiver Coverage and Limitations Handbook (July 2017)**: APD iBudget Personal Supports.

The last three items (42 CFR 438.602, Rule 59G-4.002 and the iBudget Handbook) apply only if the Agency serves Medicaid managed care or APD iBudget clients. The EVV requirement applies only to Medicaid-funded services.

### Regulators and contacts

| Regulator | Role | Contact |
|---|---|---|
| **AHCA Bureau of Health Facility Regulation, Laboratory and In-Home Services Unit** | Licenses and surveys home health agencies (skilled and non-skilled) and nurse registries; certificates of exemption | (850) 412-4500; Labstaff@ahca.myflorida.com; https://ahca.myflorida.com/health-quality-assurance/bureau-of-health-facility-regulation/laboratory-and-in-home-services/home-health-agencies.html |
| **AHCA Bureau of Health Facility Regulation, Long Term Care Services Unit** | Registers homemaker and companion services providers (AHCA Form 3110-1003) | https://ahca.myflorida.com/health-quality-assurance/hqa-applications-for-licensure.html (no phone or email listed in source) |
| **AHCA Background Screening Unit (Care Provider Background Screening Clearinghouse)** | Level 2 fingerprint screening of owners, administrators and staff | 850-412-4503; bgscreen@ahca.myflorida.com; https://ahca.myflorida.com/health-quality-assurance/bureau-of-central-services/background-screening.html |
| **AHCA Division of Medicaid, Statewide Medicaid Managed Care (SMMC) Long-Term Care** | Contracts the LTC plans that authorize and pay personal care, homemaker, companion and respite for Medicaid members | 1-877-711-3662 (choice counseling); https://ahca.myflorida.com/medicaid/statewide-medicaid-managed-care/current-smmc-program.html |

| **Florida Department of Children and Families (DCF)** | Medicaid financial eligibility; Florida Abuse Hotline | 1-800-962-2873 (Abuse Hotline); https://www.myflfamilies.com/contact-us |

Where the source lists no phone or email, use the website above to confirm current contact details. **[AGENCY NAME]** should add its own local contacts, including the county emergency management office and county health department, which the emergency plan requires.

### Official documents AHCA uses to review this manual
I found no single AHCA policy checklist or plan-of-operation form for Florida non-skilled personal care. AHCA reviews the Agency through the application forms below and through survey of compliance with Chapter 59A-8, F.A.C. The official review items in this manual are therefore built from the sections of Chapter 59A-8, F.A.C. that require written policies, plans or procedures, with item numbering following the rule text. The documents are:

- **AHCA Form 3110-1011 (April 2019)**, the home health agency license application under **Rule 59A-8.003, F.A.C.**, with the **Health Care Licensing Application Addendum (rule 59A-35.060)**. This is the source of the written-policy requirement for RN supervisor availability (non-skilled agencies) and of the satellite-office operating requirements.
- **AHCA Form 3110-1003 (December 2014)**, the homemaker and companion services registration application under **Rule 59A-8.025, F.A.C.** It is the basis for the client record, supervision plan and client-acceptance standard for the registration path.
- **Rule 59A-8.0095, F.A.C. (Personnel)**, the source of the policy and procedure, quality assurance, RN supervision, aide training and self-administered medication requirements. It also references the **Home Health Aide Competency Test, AHCA 3110-1007**.
- **Rule 59A-8.020, F.A.C. (Acceptance of Patients or Clients)**, the source of the admission, written service agreement and termination requirements.
- **Rule 59A-8.0245, F.A.C. (Advance Directives)**, the source of the required written advance-directive policies and procedures. It references AHCA's "Health Care Advance Directives – The Patients' Right to Decide."
- **Rule 59A-8.027, F.A.C. (Emergency Management Plans)**, which requires the Comprehensive Emergency Management Plan (CEMP) in the format of **AHCA Form 3110-1022 (Rev. March 2013)**. The plan is forwarded electronically to the contact designated by the Department of Health for review.

A reviewer would expect one organized policy manual, plus the CEMP, the aide training and competency documentation, a sample service agreement and a sample client record. A non-skilled agency must show RN supervision arrangements and RN supervisory visits. A director of nursing is not required for an agency without skilled care (Rule 59A-8.0095(2)(i), F.A.C.).

**Appendix A maps every official item to the policy that satisfies it.** For each item taken from the rules and forms above, Appendix A names the rule citation, the policy section and page in this manual, and the supporting document or form. Items that apply only to skilled agencies, nursing or PT services, satellite offices or LPNs are marked conditional. Items such as application forms, fees, financials, background screening and insurance are application paperwork, not manual content. They are covered in this manual only where a rule requires a written policy.

### Limits of this framework
The application forms themselves (3110-1011, 3110-1003 and 3110-1022) and AHCA's ASPEN survey tool for home health agencies were not reviewed in preparing this manual. Before relying on Appendix A, confirm the current versions of all AHCA forms and the current rule text on flrules.org (the Florida Administrative Code). Do not assume the unofficial copies are current. Rule history can change, and the Agency is responsible for following the version in force.

### Your responsibilities under this framework
- **Customize** the manual by replacing all **[AGENCY NAME]** placeholders and removing sections that do not fit the Agency's model.
- **Adopt** the manual through the governing body and record the date.
- **Keep it current** through at least annual review and prompt revision when law, forms or operations change.
- **Train staff** on the manual and document the training for every employee.

policies.title: Organization, Governing Body and Administrator Responsibilities (Non-Skilled Home Health Agency)
policies.applies_to: Governing body, owners, administrator, alternate administrator, RN supervisor and all management staff of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To define how [AGENCY NAME] is organized and governed as a Florida home health agency licensed for non-skilled services, and to state who is accountable for licensure compliance, qualified management, the quality of hands-on personal care delivered by home health aides and CNAs, and the accuracy of what the agency tells AHCA.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] operates under Part III of Chapter 400, F.S. (C1) as a home health agency licensed to provide non-skilled services only. Hands-on personal care is delivered by home health aides and CNAs (s. 400.462, F.S., C2). Companions and homemakers do not provide hands-on personal care (s. 400.462, F.S., C2). The governing body is legally responsible for the agency and appoints a qualified administrator who manages daily operations. The administrator must meet s. 400.462(1) and s. 400.476(1), F.S. (C2, C5). That means the administrator is a Florida-licensed physician, physician assistant or registered nurse, or has at least one year of supervisory or administrative experience in home health care or in a licensed facility. A director of nursing is not required while the agency provides no skilled nursing (s. 400.476(2), F.S., C5; Rule 59A-8.0095(2)(i), F.A.C., C17). If skilled nursing or LPN services are added, the agency will first meet the requirements in SVC-14. A registered nurse still assigns personal care tasks and makes supervisory visits to clients receiving aide services (Rule 59A-8.0095(3), F.A.C., C17). The license application states which services are provided directly by employees and which are provided by contract, and the agency provides at least one service directly to clients (Rule 59A-8.008(4), F.A.C., C23). Statute and rule set no staffing ratios or caseload limits (s. 400.476, F.S., C5). The agency therefore sets its own RN-hour and supervisory-visit standards in SVC-06 and SVC-07 and reviews them in GOV-07. No services are advertised or delivered that are not on the license (see GOV-03).

Hands-on personal care by home health aides and CNAs, plus homemaker and companion services. No skilled nursing or other skilled therapies are provided.
Hands-on help with activities of daily living such as bathing, dressing, eating, hygiene and transfers (s. 400.462, F.S., C2).
The registered nurse who assigns personal care tasks, makes supervisory visits and keeps full responsibility for those assignments (Rule 59A-8.0095(3), F.A.C., C17).

procedures: The governing body adopts a written resolution at formation that names the agency's licensed service scope as non-skilled home health services and records that no skilled nursing is provided. The resolution is dated and filed in the governance binder.

The governing body appoints the administrator in writing. Before appointment, the governing body reviews and files the administrator's proof of qualification under s. 400.462(1) and s. 400.476(1), F.S.: a Florida license (physician, PA or RN), or documented work history showing at least one year of supervisory or administrative experience in home health care or a licensed facility.
The administrator completes level 2 background screening before assuming duties (see PER-03). The governing body does not allow the administrator to start until a clear result is on file.

The administrator signs a job description acknowledging responsibility for compliance with Part III of Chapter 400, F.S., and Chapter 59A-8, F.A.C. The signed description is kept in the administrator's personnel file.
The administrator designates a written on-site alternate according to GOV-02 and reviews the designation at least annually and whenever staffing changes.

The administrator verifies that the license application and any later change filing state explicitly which services are provided directly by employees and which are provided by contract. At least one service, hands-on aide service, must be provided directly by [AGENCY NAME] employees (Rule 59A-8.008(4), F.A.C.). The administrator keeps a copy of the filed statement in the license file.

Before any contracted service is arranged, the administrator reviews the proposed contract for agency responsibility. The agency keeps responsibility for the quality of contracted services (see SVC-15 for ALF and adult family care home arrangements and contracted staff).

The governing body designates a registered nurse as RN supervisor. The RN supervisor assigns personal care tasks to aides and performs supervisory visits under SVC-05, SVC-06 and SVC-07. The RN supervisor keeps full responsibility for the tasks the RN assigns (Rule 59A-8.0095(3), F.A.C.).

The administrator confirms that no director of nursing position is needed because no skilled care is provided, and records this finding in the governance binder. If skilled nursing, LPN or other skilled services are ever proposed, the administrator stops and follows SVC-14 before taking any step toward delivering those services.

The administrator sets and documents agency staffing standards: caseload per aide, RN supervisory-visit intervals and RN hours. These are agency standards, because no state ratios exist. The standards are reviewed under GOV-07 at least quarterly in the first year and annually after that.

If the administrator changes, the governing body appoints a replacement who meets s. 400.462(1) and s. 400.476(1), F.S. The new administrator completes level 2 screening. The agency notifies AHCA of the change as required by Rule 59A-8.0095(1)(b), F.A.C. (see GOV-10), and files the notice and screening result in the license file.

The governing body meets at least [FREQUENCY, e.g., quarterly] and reviews: survey and complaint results, QA findings (GOV-07), incident trends (SAF-02), grievance trends (CR-02), financial status (GOV-03), and policy updates (GOV-06). Minutes are signed and dated.
The administrator makes the license, current policy manuals and organization chart available to AHCA surveyors on request (see GOV-09).
The administrator reviews this policy annually with the governing body and records the review date and any change in the governance binder.

responsibilities.duty: Holds legal responsibility for the agency; appoints a qualified administrator; approves the service scope and policies; reviews QA, financial and compliance reports; and ensures the agency does not offer services outside its license.

Manages daily operations; keeps the license and personnel requirements current; maintains the policy manuals; supervises management staff; files required notices with AHCA; and keeps records open to surveyors.
Acts with full authority for daily operations when the administrator is absent (GOV-02).
Assigns personal care tasks, performs supervisory visits and documents RN oversight of aides (SVC-05 to SVC-07).
Work within the agency's licensed scope and report any request to provide services not offered to the administrator.

documentation: Governing body resolution and appointment letter
Administrator qualification evidence and level 2 screening result
Signed administrator job description
Organization chart and statement of direct versus contracted services
Governing body meeting minutes
Record of annual policy review
Staffing standards document (supervisory-visit intervals, caseloads, RN hours)

policies.title: Alternate Administrator and Business-Hours Availability
policies.applies_to: Administrator, alternate administrator, office staff and RN supervisor of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To ensure that a qualified, authorized manager is always responsible for the agency, and that the public and AHCA can reach the administrator or alternate during the business hours the rules require.
policies.policy: This policy meets Rule 59A-8.0095(1)(a)2, F.A.C. (written designation of an on-site alternate administrator for the administrator's absences). [AGENCY NAME] designates in writing an on-site alternate administrator who has responsibility and authority for daily operation of the agency during the administrator's absences and who meets the qualifications in s. 400.462(1) and s. 400.476(1), F.S. (C5, C17). The administrator or the alternate is available to the public for any 8 consecutive hours between 7:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m., Monday through Friday (Rule 59A-8.003(9)(a), F.A.C., C16). A staff person answers the telephone and the door during those hours and can reach the administrator (Rule 59A-8.003(9)(b), C16). The office is open during the hours stated on the license application. Surveyor-access timeframes are in GOV-09 and RN supervisor availability is in SVC-07.

definitions.definition: A person designated in writing to act with the administrator's authority and responsibility at the agency premises during the administrator's absence.
The office hours posted on the license application, which include at least 8 consecutive hours between 7:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m., Monday through Friday.
Reachable in person or by telephone by clients, families, referral sources and AHCA, with a staff person present to answer the phone and door.

procedures: The administrator selects an alternate who meets s. 400.462(1) and s. 400.476(1), F.S. and collects proof of qualification. Proof means a Florida license or documentation of at least one year of supervisory or administrative experience in home health care or a licensed facility.
The alternate completes background screening under PER-03 before designation. A clear result is placed in the personnel file.

The administrator completes a written designation form. It states the alternate's name and title, the effective date, and the alternate's responsibility and authority for daily operation of the agency during the administrator's absences. Both the administrator and the alternate sign it.
The designation form is placed in the license file and the personnel file of the alternate. A copy is posted in the administrator's office binder for surveyor review.

The administrator sets the office hours to include at least 8 consecutive hours between 7:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m., Monday through Friday, and records those hours as [OFFICE HOURS] in the license file. Office hours match the hours stated to AHCA.

The administrator creates a weekly schedule showing who is the administrator or alternate on site for each business-hours day. Each day is covered by one of the two. The administrator keeps the schedule for at least [RETENTION PERIOD] in the license file.

A receptionist or other designated staff person answers the telephone and the door during office hours and knows how to reach the administrator immediately by [PHONE] or the alternate's number. The administrator reviews this expectation with each office staff member at hire.

The posted business hours and the main phone number [PHONE] appear at the entrance, on the agency's website and on voicemail. After-hours voicemail gives the on-call number for client emergencies (see SVC-09 and SVC-11).

When the administrator is absent, the alternate acts with full authority. The alternate documents any significant decision in the administrator-absence log, and the administrator reviews the log on return.

If the alternate leaves the agency or no longer qualifies, the administrator names a new qualified alternate and completes a new written designation immediately. The agency never operates without a designated alternate.

If the administrator and alternate are both unexpectedly unavailable, the staff person on duty calls the administrator or alternate by phone at once and the administrator arranges coverage the same day. The event is recorded in the absence log.
The administrator tests availability by calling the office at random during business hours at least quarterly and recording the result. Failures are corrected and reported through GOV-07.
The administrator reviews the alternate designation, schedule and posted hours annually and after any staff change, and records the review date in the license file.

responsibilities.duty: Designates a qualified alternate in writing, sets and posts office hours, and ensures daily coverage Monday through Friday.
Acts with the administrator's authority during absences, is on site as scheduled, and documents decisions in the absence log.
Answer the phone and door during business hours and can reach the administrator.
Verifies at its meetings that an alternate is designated and that coverage hours are met.

documentation: Written alternate administrator designation signed by both parties
Alternate's qualification evidence and screening result
Posted office hours and weekly coverage schedule
Administrator-absence log
Quarterly availability test records

policies.title: Licensure Track, Service Area, Advertising, Insurance and Financial Ability Requirements
policies.applies_to: Governing body, administrator, marketing and admissions staff of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To ensure that [AGENCY NAME] holds the correct Florida license or registration for every service it offers, advertises only what is authorized, and keeps the required insurance and financial capacity.
policies.policy: Under Part III of Chapter 400, F.S. (C1), a license is required to provide hands-on personal care (s. 400.464, F.S., C3). Hands-on care may be provided under a Home Health Agency license, which can be limited to non-skilled services, or through a Nurse Registry. Companions and homemakers may not provide hands-on personal care, and companion-only or homemaker-only providers must register under s. 400.509, F.S. (C2, C10). [AGENCY NAME] does not serve clients before its license or registration is issued. [AGENCY NAME] does not advertise any service that is not on its license, because doing so is unlicensed activity (s. 400.464, F.S., C3). The license number, or the registration number for a registered provider, appears in every advertisement, website page and business card (s. 400.464, F.S., C3; s. 400.509(5), F.S., C10). The agency keeps malpractice and liability insurance of at least $250,000 per claim and proves it with its initial and each renewal application (s. 400.471, F.S., C4). It documents financial ability with CPA-compiled two-year projections and maintains startup, working-capital and contingency funds covering at least three months of projected expenses, with contingency of at least one month (s. 400.471, C4; s. 408.8065, C15). If any controlling interest is a nonimmigrant alien, the agency posts the surety bond required by s. 408.8065(2), F.S. (C15). As a non-skilled agency, [AGENCY NAME] is exempt from accreditation (s. 400.471, F.S., C4). Nurse-registry referrals are independent contractors that the registry may not supervise (s. 400.506, F.S., C9, nurse registry defined in s. 400.462, C2). [AGENCY NAME] operates under the employer model described in this manual and does not operate a nurse registry. Any advertising of special Alzheimer's care is accompanied by the disclosure required by s. 400.4785(2), F.S. (C6).

definitions.definition: The type of state authorization under which a service line operates: Home Health Agency license (non-skilled), Homemaker and Companion registration, or Nurse Registry license.
Providing or advertising services that require a license when the license is not held or does not list those services (s. 400.464, F.S.).
A business that refers independent-contractor caregivers to clients and does not supervise them (s. 400.462, F.S.; s. 400.506, F.S.). It is a separate license and not part of this manual.
An ownership or control position in the agency. If it is held by a nonimmigrant alien, a $500,000 surety bond is required (s. 408.8065(2), F.S.).

procedures: Before launching, the governing body decides in writing which service lines the agency will offer and confirms the track for each: Home Health Agency license (hands-on personal care plus homemaker/companion), registration only (companion/homemaker only, see GOV-04), or neither.

The administrator prepares the license application on the AHCA form with the required addendum, listing non-skilled services only, and states the counties to be served. The administrator confirms the application also states direct versus contracted services (see GOV-01).

The administrator obtains CPA-compiled two-year financial projections and documents startup, working-capital and contingency funds covering at least three months of projected expenses, with contingency of at least one month. The CPA letter and bank evidence are placed in the license file.

The administrator obtains malpractice and liability policies of at least $250,000 per claim each and files the certificates with the application. Certificates are checked for correct named insured, address and dates.

The administrator checks the ownership and controlling-interest disclosure. If any controlling interest is held by a nonimmigrant alien, the administrator obtains the $500,000 surety bond under s. 408.8065(2), F.S., before submission.

The administrator confirms with the governing body that the agency does not claim accreditation and does not describe itself as accredited. Accreditation is not required for a non-skilled agency (s. 400.471, F.S.).

No client is admitted and no hands-on care is delivered until AHCA issues the license. The licensure survey is completed first (s. 400.471, F.S.). The administrator records the license number, effective date and expiration date in the license file and on a calendar with renewal reminders [DAYS] days before expiration.

The administrator reviews all advertising (print, web, social media, directories, business cards, vehicle signs, brochures, e-mail signatures) before publication. Each item must show the license number, list only licensed services and match the license. The review is initialed and dated.

If the agency also offers companion-only service under registration, the administrator confirms the registration is issued first and follows GOV-04. Marketing materials distinguish the companion service (no hands-on help) from licensed personal care and show the correct number for each.

If the agency wants to advertise Alzheimer's or dementia-related special care, the administrator first prepares the disclosure of the services that make it suitable (s. 400.4785(2), F.S.) and ensures staff training under PER-05. Without that disclosure, no such claim is made.
The administrator monitors insurance expiration dates and renews coverage at least [DAYS] days before expiration. Proof of insurance is submitted at each license renewal (s. 400.471, F.S.).

The administrator reports monthly cash and contingency-fund balances to the governing body. If funds fall below the amount that supports three months of projected expenses, the governing body is notified immediately and a written recovery plan is adopted.

If any staff member or other person receives a referral request for a service not on the license, such as skilled nursing or wound care, the request is declined and referred to a licensed provider. The administrator logs the request, and SVC-14 applies if the agency considers adding that service.
The administrator reviews licensure tracks, ads, insurance and funding annually, and whenever a service is changed, and records the review in the license file.

responsibilities.duty: Selects the licensure track, funds the agency as required, and approves financial and insurance status.
Files applications and renewals, keeps insurance and bond current, reviews all advertising, and prevents unlicensed activity.
Use only approved materials with the license or registration number, and decline services not on the license.
Prepares the compiled projections and supports financial documentation.

documentation: License or registration certificate and renewal calendar
CPA-compiled two-year projections and funding evidence
Insurance certificates (malpractice and liability) and surety bond, if applicable
Advertising review log with approved samples
Alzheimer's care disclosure, if used
Declined-service log
Annual licensure-track review

policies.title: Homemaker and Companion Services Registration and Geographic Service Area (companion-only service line)
policies.applies_to: Administrator, intake staff and homemaker/companion supervisors of [AGENCY NAME] (only if a registered companion/homemaker service line is operated)
policies.purpose: To ensure that any companion-only or homemaker-only service line is registered with AHCA before services begin, stays within its approved geographic service area, and never provides hands-on personal care.
policies.policy: This policy meets Rule 59A-8.025(6), F.A.C. (homemaker/companion registration: the application states the specific geographic area to be served). It applies only if [AGENCY NAME] offers companion-only or homemaker-only services under registration. A licensed home health agency is exempt from registering (Rule 59A-8.025(1), F.A.C., C21), so a licensed [AGENCY NAME] does not need separate registration for these services. Homemaker and companion providers must register under s. 400.509, F.S. (C10), before providing services (Rule 59A-8.025(1), C21). The application on AHCA Form 3110-1003 states the specific geographic area to be served. That area is the counties within the health service planning district of the address of record (Rule 59A-8.025(6), C21). A registrant that held a registration as of July 1, 2015 may keep serving the counties listed on that registration if a plan for supervising staff working outside the primary geographic service area is documented (Rule 59A-8.025(6), C21). Registration is filed biennially, and the renewal or change-of-ownership application is submitted at least 60 days before expiration (Rule 59A-8.025(2)-(3), C21). The registration fee is $50 per biennium under statute, adjusted for CPI (s. 400.509, C10). Registrants do not provide hands-on personal care. The registration number appears in every advertisement (s. 400.509(5), F.S., C10). Each worker's employment history is verified before service (s. 400.509(4), F.S., C10). Diligent effort means two documented attempts to verify employment or contractual history (Rule 59A-8.025(7), C21). The agency accepts a client only if the services can be provided adequately and safely, and supplies capable staff for all scheduled visits (Rule 59A-8.025(9), C21).

definitions.definition: AHCA authorization for providers whose services are exempt from licensure, because they do not provide hands-on care, to offer homemaker and companion services (s. 400.509, F.S.).
The counties within the health service planning district of the address of record (Rule 59A-8.025(6), F.A.C.).
Non-hands-on services such as light housekeeping, meal preparation, errands, reminders and companionship. Hands-on personal care is excluded (see SVC-02).
Two documented attempts to verify a worker's employment or contractual history (Rule 59A-8.025(7), F.A.C.).

procedures: The governing body decides whether the agency will offer a registered homemaker/companion line. If the agency holds a Home Health Agency license, it records that no separate registration is needed under Rule 59A-8.025(1), F.A.C. If it does not hold a license, it proceeds with registration.

The administrator completes AHCA Form 3110-1003 and pays the registration fee ($50 per biennium under statute, CPI-adjusted). The administrator files the form with the Long Term Care Services Unit of AHCA's Bureau of Health Facility Regulation and keeps a copy in the registration file.

On the application, the administrator lists the specific counties to be served. Those counties lie within the health service planning district of the agency's address of record (Rule 59A-8.025(6), F.A.C.). The list is saved in the registration file as the approved service area.

If the agency held a registration on July 1, 2015 and wants to continue serving counties listed on it outside the primary service area, the administrator writes a plan for supervising staff working there. The plan states who supervises, how often and by what means. The administrator keeps the plan with the registration.

The agency does not provide services, accept referrals for service dates, or advertise until AHCA issues the registration. The administrator records the registration number and dates, and places a renewal reminder at least 90 days before expiration.
The administrator files the renewal or change-of-ownership application at least 60 days before the registration expires (Rule 59A-8.025(2), F.A.C.). The administrator keeps proof of filing.

Intake staff check each referral's service address against the approved county list. Referrals outside the approved list are declined and referred to another registered or licensed provider unless the supervision plan above covers the county.

Before assigning any worker, the administrator verifies employment history (s. 400.509(4), F.S.). For each worker, two documented attempts are made to verify prior employment or contractual history, and the results (date, method, person contacted, response) are recorded in the personnel file as diligent effort (Rule 59A-8.025(7), F.A.C.). See PER-03 and PER-07.

Intake staff screen every request against SVC-02. If the client needs bathing, dressing, toileting assistance, feeding, transfers or other hands-on help, the registered line does not accept the request. The request is declined and referred, or served only under the agency's home health license, if held.

The administrator accepts a client only after determining that services can be provided adequately and safely, and then ensures capable staff are scheduled for every visit (Rule 59A-8.025(9), F.A.C.). The determination is recorded in the client record (REC-02).
The registration number is placed on all ads, the website, contracts and business cards. The administrator reviews each item under GOV-03 before publication.
The administrator audits service-area compliance quarterly by comparing client addresses with the approved counties. Exceptions are corrected and reported under GOV-07.
The administrator reviews this policy annually, and whenever the address, ownership or counties change. Address and county changes are handled under GOV-10.

responsibilities.duty: Files and renews registration on time, defines the service area, verifies employment histories, and keeps the line limited to non-hands-on services.
Screen referrals for service area and hands-on needs before acceptance.
Supervises staff, including staff working outside the primary service area under the supervision plan.
Approves the decision to operate the registered service line and receives service-area audit results.

documentation: AHCA Form 3110-1003 and registration certificate
Approved county list and any supervision plan for out-of-area staff
Renewal filing proof and calendar
Employment-history verification and diligent-effort records
Intake screening and declination log
Quarterly service-area audit

policies.title: Satellite Offices and Drop-Off Sites (conditional)
policies.applies_to: Administrator, alternate, RN supervisor and satellite or drop-off site staff of [AGENCY NAME]. This policy applies only if the agency opens a satellite office or drop-off site.
policies.purpose: To make sure any satellite office or drop-off site of [AGENCY NAME] is established lawfully within its geographic service area and is managed so that care, supervision, records and public access are equal to the main office.
policies.policy: This policy meets Rule 59A-8.003(6)(a)-(h), F.A.C. and is conditional on the agency having a satellite office. A satellite office is an office in the same geographic service area as the main office and is not separately licensed (Rule 59A-8.003(5), F.A.C., C16). For each satellite office, [AGENCY NAME] will: (a) ensure coverage of professional staff based on projected clients; (b) coordinate care and services by staff; (c) ensure supervision and service provision when staff are absent; (d) maintain communication and integration of services between the main and satellite offices; (e) provide access to patient records at the satellite office; (f) monitor daily clinical and administrative activities, services, personnel and administrative issues; (g) ensure periodic onsite visits by the administrator; and (h) make the satellite office's hours available to the public if they differ from the main office. Opening or closing an office, or changing address or counties served, requires AHCA Form 3110-1011 with zoning and right-to-occupy evidence (Rule 59A-8.003(8), C16). Drop-off sites are used only within the conditions of Rule 59A-8.003(7), F.A.C. (C16). If the agency has no satellite office, this policy is not implemented but remains in the manual.

definitions.definition: An additional office of [AGENCY NAME] in the same geographic service area as the main office; it is not separately licensed (Rule 59A-8.003(5), F.A.C.).
A site used by the agency under Rule 59A-8.003(7), F.A.C. It is not a satellite office and is used only within the conditions of that rule.
The licensed address of [AGENCY NAME]: [ADDRESS].

procedures: Before opening any satellite office, the governing body approves it in writing. The administrator confirms the proposed location is within the same geographic service area as the main office.

The administrator files AHCA Form 3110-1011 to report the new office, with zoning and right-to-occupy evidence (Rule 59A-8.003(8), F.A.C.), and opens it only after the filing is submitted and any AHCA response is received. A copy is kept in the license file. See GOV-10.

Staff coverage (item a): The administrator projects the number of clients to be served from the satellite office. The administrator assigns RN supervisor time, aides and office staff in proportion to that projection, and records the staffing plan. The plan is reviewed at least quarterly and whenever the census changes by [PERCENT] or more.

Coordination of care (item b): The administrator names a satellite lead. The lead coordinates schedules, service plans and communication with the RN supervisor and ensures every client has an assigned case manager at the main office.

Supervision when staff are absent (item c): The satellite lead and the administrator keep a written coverage plan that names back-up aides and an RN supervisor for each client. If a staff member is absent, the lead arranges coverage under SVC-09 and notifies the administrator the same day.

Communication and integration (item d): The main and satellite offices use the same forms, policies, scheduling system and client records. The administrator and satellite lead hold a documented check-in at least [FREQUENCY, e.g., weekly], with minutes kept.

Access to records (item e): Client records are accessible at the satellite office through [RECORD SYSTEM, e.g., secure electronic record] with role-based access under CR-04 and REC-01. If paper records are kept there, they are in a locked cabinet. A surveyor at the satellite office can view any client record kept there on request.

Monitoring (item f): The administrator reviews a weekly report of visits, missed visits, incidents, complaints, personnel actions and billing from the satellite. Findings are recorded and trends are reported to GOV-07.

Administrator visits (item g): The administrator visits the satellite office on site at least [FREQUENCY, e.g., monthly], observes operations, reviews records and talks with staff. Each visit is logged with date, findings and corrective actions.

Public hours (item h): If the satellite office's hours differ from the main office hours, they are posted at the satellite entrance, on the website and on the agency's voicemail, and kept in the license file. If the hours are identical, the administrator records that no separate posting is needed.
Staff at the satellite office follow the same business-hours telephone and door-answering expectations as GOV-02, and a staff person can reach the administrator during hours of operation.

If a drop-off site is used, the administrator first reviews the conditions of Rule 59A-8.003(7), F.A.C., documents that the planned use meets them, and keeps the finding in the license file. No client records are stored at a drop-off site unless that rule allows it.

To close a satellite office or change its address or counties served, the administrator files AHCA Form 3110-1011 (Rule 59A-8.003(8)). Before closing, client records and supervision duties are moved to the main office and clients are told of any change in contact information.
The administrator reviews this policy annually and updates it whenever the satellite structure changes.

responsibilities.duty: Approves opening and closing of satellite offices and receives satellite performance reports.
Files AHCA changes, sets staffing, monitors operations, and visits the satellite office on schedule.
Coordinates daily services, staff coverage, record access and communication with the main office.
Supervises aides and conducts supervisory visits for satellite clients.

documentation: Governing body approval and AHCA Form 3110-1011 with zoning and occupancy evidence
Satellite staffing and coverage plan
Coordination meeting minutes
Administrator satellite visit log
Weekly monitoring reports
Posted hours notice, if different from main office
Drop-off site determination, if used

policies.title: Policy Review and Document Control (Agency Procedure and Client Care Policy Manuals)
policies.applies_to: Administrator, alternate administrator, RN supervisor and all employees of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To keep the agency's procedure and client care policy manuals current, approved, version-controlled, known to staff and available to surveyors.
policies.policy: This policy meets Rule 59A-8.0095(2)(a)4, F.A.C. The rule requires a director of nursing to maintain and adhere to agency procedure and patient care policy manuals. That duty is not required of an agency that does not provide skilled care (Rule 59A-8.0095(2)(i), F.A.C., C17). Because [AGENCY NAME] provides no skilled care and has no director of nursing, the administrator maintains and adheres to the agency procedure manual and the client care policy manual, with RN supervisor input on client care policies. If skilled care is added, the director of nursing will take on this duty (see SVC-14). The manuals are reviewed at least annually and after any amendment to Chapter 59A-8, F.A.C. Rules 59A-8.003 and 59A-8.0095, F.A.C. were amended in 2026, so the administrator checks the current text on flrules.org rather than relying on older copies (C16, C17). Every version is logged and each employee signs an acknowledgment. A current manual is kept at the office and produced to a surveyor on request (see GOV-09).

definitions.definition: The written administrative policies and procedures of [AGENCY NAME] (governance, personnel, records, safety).
The written policies and procedures that govern services to clients, including scope of services, service plans, supervision and discharge.
A record of each policy's version number, date approved, summary of change and approver.
An employee's signed and dated statement that they received, read and understand the manual and its updates.

procedures: The governing body adopts the manuals at initial licensure and signs an approval page showing the date and version number.

The administrator is the manual owner. The administrator keeps one controlled master copy, in electronic form with a printed or accessible copy at the office at [ADDRESS], and records its location in the license file.
The administrator keeps a version log for every policy showing policy ID, title, version, date approved, a summary of changes, and the approver's name.
Each policy shows its ID, version and last-review date in the footer so that outdated copies are easily recognized.

At least annually, the administrator and RN supervisor review every policy against current law and rules. They check the current text of Chapter 400 Part III, F.S. and Chapter 59A-8, F.A.C. on the Florida Senate and flrules.org sites, noting that Rules 59A-8.003 and 59A-8.0095 were amended in 2026. The review date and reviewer names are recorded.

The administrator also reviews the manual within [NUMBER, e.g., 30] days after any statute or rule amendment, after any AHCA survey finding, and after any incident or QA finding that shows a policy gap (see GOV-07).

Proposed changes are drafted by the administrator, reviewed by the RN supervisor for client care policies, and approved by the governing body or its designee. Changes are not used until approved and the version log is updated.
After approval, the administrator removes superseded versions from active use, archives them in the version history for at least [RETENTION PERIOD], and distributes the new version to staff.

Each employee signs an acknowledgment of the manual at hire. This is part of orientation under PER-04, and the acknowledgment is placed in the personnel file (PER-07). Employees sign a new acknowledgment for each material policy change within [NUMBER, e.g., 14] days of distribution.
The administrator trains staff on material changes before they take effect, and documents training dates and attendance on a sign-in sheet.

Policies are available to staff at all times, including aides in the field through [METHOD, e.g., mobile app or printed field guide], and to clients on request to the extent they relate to client rights and complaints.
A current, complete copy of both manuals is kept at the office. When a surveyor arrives, the administrator or alternate produces the manuals and version log without delay (see GOV-09).
The administrator tracks the review calendar and reports overdue reviews to the governing body. At the annual governing body review, the administrator presents the changes made during the year.

If skilled care is ever added, the administrator transfers manual maintenance responsibility to the director of nursing as required by Rule 59A-8.0095(2)(a)4, F.A.C., and the governing body approves the changes under SVC-14.

responsibilities.duty: Approves the manuals and substantive changes and receives the annual review report.
Maintains and adheres to the manuals, controls versions, performs annual and rule-change reviews, and ensures employee acknowledgments.
Reviews client care policies for clinical accuracy and consistency with delegation and supervision practice.
Read, follow and sign acknowledgment of the manuals and updates.
