policies.applies_to: Home health aides, certified nursing assistants (CNAs), the RN Supervisor, the Administrator and scheduling staff of [AGENCY NAME] (Home Health Agency license limited to non-skilled services)
policies.purpose: To define the tasks that [AGENCY NAME]'s home health aides and CNAs may perform, the tasks they may never perform, and how the agency keeps staff within those limits, so that clients receive safe hands-on personal care and the agency stays within its non-skilled license.
policies.policy:
[AGENCY NAME] provides only non-skilled services: hands-on personal care by home health aides and CNAs, plus homemaker and companion services (see SVC-02). Home health aides provide hands-on personal care under s. 400.462, F.S. Aides and CNAs work only within the written assignment of a licensed health professional and within this policy.

This policy meets Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(l), F.A.C. (Home Health Aide and CNA Responsibilities). Aides and CNAs may: (1) perform personal care activities in a written assignment by a licensed health professional; (2) maintain a clean, safe and healthy environment; (3) perform other activities taught by a licensed professional for a specific client, limited to the tasks listed in the rule; (4) keep records of personal health care activities; (5) observe and report the client's appearance and gross behavioral changes to the RN; and (6) supervise self-administered medication, limited to the four steps listed in the rule (see SVC-08).

This policy meets Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(p), F.A.C. (Responsibilities Aides and CNAs May Not Perform). Aides and CNAs may not perform any task listed in that paragraph, which begins with therapeutic services that require licensure. The agency also prohibits, without exception: giving injectable medications; administering anything by tube; mixing or calculating medication doses; and giving PRN (as-needed) medications that require judgment about whether or when to give them. The agency adopts the full list in Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(p) as its prohibited-task list; the verbatim current rule text is kept in the Policy Manual as Attachment SVC-01-A and is reviewed under GOV-06.

The license application states which services the agency provides directly through employees and which by contract, and the agency provides at least one service directly to clients (Rule 59A-8.023 is not relied on here; see Rule 59A-8.008(4), F.A.C.). Contracted caregivers are held to this same scope.

An aide or CNA who is asked to do a prohibited task must decline politely, keep the client safe, and call the RN Supervisor.

definitions.definition: Hands-on help with activities of daily living such as bathing, dressing, eating, personal hygiene and transfers, as defined in s. 400.462, F.S.

An unlicensed caregiver who meets the qualifications in PER-01 and PER-02 (current Florida CNA certification, or the required 40 hours of training or a passed competency test) and who provides hands-on personal care.
Any task listed in Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(p), F.A.C., or in this policy, that an aide or CNA may not perform.
The individualized, dated assignment sheet prepared or approved by the RN that lists the tasks an aide or CNA may do for a specific client.
A clearly noticeable change in the client's mood, behavior, alertness or orientation that the aide must report to the RN.

procedures: Before adoption of this manual, the Administrator attaches the verbatim current text of Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(l) (including its list of permitted tasks) and Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(p) (the complete prohibited-task list) as Attachment SVC-01-A, and records the date checked. The Administrator re-checks the attachment against the rule at each annual policy review under GOV-06.

The RN Supervisor prepares a written assignment sheet for every aide or CNA assigned to a client, listing only tasks that are within Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(l) and appropriate to that client and caregiver.

The RN Supervisor confirms from the personnel file (PER-07) that the caregiver has current CNA certification or the 40-hour training or passed competency test, and the 2-hour medication-assistance training, before the caregiver's first visit.

Any task taught by a licensed professional for a specific client is taught by the RN Supervisor or another licensed professional, is limited to the tasks listed in the rule, and is documented in the client file with the date, the task, the person who taught it and the caregiver's return demonstration.
At orientation (PER-04), the RN Supervisor gives each caregiver a copy of the permitted and prohibited task lists and has the caregiver sign an acknowledgment filed in the personnel record.
At each visit, the aide or CNA records the personal care activities performed, the time in and out, and the client's response in the visit record (see SVC-10 and REC-01).

The aide or CNA observes the client's appearance and behavior and reports any change in appearance or any gross behavioral change to the RN Supervisor by phone the same day, and immediately if the client is in danger (see SVC-11).

The aide or CNA supervises self-administered medication only within the four steps listed in Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(l), only after the client has been informed and has given written consent, and only as described in SVC-08.

If a client, family member or other person asks an aide or CNA to perform a prohibited task, the caregiver declines, does not perform any part of it, ensures the client is safe, and notifies the RN Supervisor before leaving the home or within one hour.

The RN Supervisor evaluates each request for a prohibited task within one business day. The RN Supervisor tells the client or representative what the agency can and cannot do, and either updates the service plan (SVC-04) with an allowed alternative, refers the client to a properly licensed provider, or begins the process in SVC-14 if the client needs skilled services.

The RN Supervisor reviews visit records and conducts supervisory visits (SVC-06) to verify caregivers are working within their assignments, and corrects any out-of-scope practice by retraining the same week and documenting the retraining.

A caregiver who performs a prohibited task is removed from the affected client assignment pending review, and the RN Supervisor notifies the Administrator the same day. The Administrator completes an incident report under SAF-02, ensures client safety, and applies corrective action under PER-09. Reportable events are reported under REC-03.
The Administrator reviews every out-of-scope request and every violation at least quarterly as part of Quality Assurance (GOV-07).
The Administrator keeps the application's statement of which services are provided directly versus by contract current, and notifies AHCA of any change under GOV-10.

responsibilities.duty: Keeps the scope of services consistent with the license; maintains Attachment SVC-01-A; investigates violations; ensures at least one service is provided directly by employees.
Prepares written assignments; teaches client-specific tasks; responds to caregiver questions and out-of-scope requests; supervises caregivers.
Perform only permitted tasks; decline prohibited tasks; document personal care; observe and report changes.
Do not accept or schedule requests for tasks outside this policy and route them to the RN Supervisor.

documentation: Attachment SVC-01-A: verbatim Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(l) and (5)(p), with date verified
Written assignment sheets in the client file
Caregiver acknowledgment of permitted and prohibited tasks (personnel file)
Records of client-specific task teaching and return demonstrations
Visit records of personal care activities performed
Records of declined requests, RN responses and any corrective action
Incident reports under SAF-02, where applicable

policies.title: Homemaker and Companion Duties and Limits (no hands-on care)
policies.applies_to: Homemakers, companions, the Administrator, the RN Supervisor and scheduling staff of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To define what homemakers and companions may do, to prohibit hands-on personal care by these workers, and to set the steps for moving a client to an aide or CNA when hands-on help is needed.
policies.policy:
Companions and homemakers may not provide hands-on personal care (s. 400.462, F.S.). [AGENCY NAME] follows Rule 59A-8.0095(12), F.A.C., for homemaker and companion duties.

Homemaker duties are housekeeping, meal preparation, laundry, shopping and cosmetic assistance. Companion duties are providing company, escorting the client, and keeping a written service record. Homemakers and companions may only verbally remind a client about medication; they may not open containers, hand the client medication, or give any other help with medication.

Hands-on personal care (bathing, dressing, eating, personal hygiene and transfers) may be provided only by a home health aide or CNA working under an RN-supervised service plan (see SVC-01, SVC-04 and SVC-06). If a client who is receiving homemaker or companion services needs hands-on help, the agency reassigns the client to an aide or CNA under the procedures below.

If [AGENCY NAME] holds a home health agency license, it is exempt from separate homemaker and companion registration; if it provides companion-only services it is registered with AHCA under Rule 59A-8.025, F.A.C., and follows GOV-04. Either way, these limits apply to every homemaker and companion.

definitions.definition: A worker who performs housekeeping, meal preparation, laundry, shopping and cosmetic assistance, without hands-on personal care.
A worker who provides company and escort and keeps a written service record, without hands-on personal care.
Physical help with bathing, dressing, eating, personal hygiene, toileting or transfers; it may be provided only by a home health aide or CNA.
Telling the client that it is time to take medication, with no physical help of any kind.

procedures: At hire, the Administrator tells every homemaker and companion in writing that hands-on personal care is prohibited and that they may only give verbal medication reminders; the worker signs an acknowledgment kept in the personnel file (PER-07).

At intake (SVC-03), the intake coordinator identifies whether the client needs any hands-on help. If so, the client is accepted only for aide or CNA services, with RN-supervised service planning; if not, the client may be accepted for homemaker or companion services.

The service plan for each homemaker or companion client (SVC-04) lists the permitted duties by type (housekeeping, meal preparation, laundry, shopping, cosmetic assistance, company, escort) and states that no hands-on care will be provided.
The homemaker or companion completes a written service record at every visit with the date, time in and out, and services performed, and signs it. The records are filed in the client record (REC-02).
The worker gives only a verbal reminder at medication time and records that a reminder was given. The worker does not touch, open, hand over, measure or place medication.
If a client asks for help with bathing, dressing, eating, hygiene or transfers, the worker declines, ensures the client is safe, and phones the RN Supervisor or scheduling staff the same day.
If the client falls, appears ill or is in danger, the worker follows SVC-11 and calls 911 first when there is an emergency, without providing hands-on care other than what is needed to summon help.

Within one business day of a report of unmet hands-on needs, the RN Supervisor contacts the client or representative and arranges an RN assessment visit, with the client's written consent for the RN to enter the home.

If hands-on help is needed, the RN Supervisor writes an RN-supervised service plan and a written assignment (SVC-04, SVC-05), and scheduling staff assign a qualified aide or CNA. The homemaker or companion continues only with the allowed duties.
The service agreement is updated and signed by the client or representative and an agency representative before hands-on care begins (CR-07).

If no qualified aide or CNA is available, scheduling staff tell the client right away, continue only non-hands-on duties, and refer the client to another provider under SVC-12 if safe care cannot be assured.

If a homemaker or companion is found to have provided hands-on care, the Administrator removes the worker from hands-on situations, documents an incident under SAF-02, retrains or disciplines the worker (PER-09) and reviews the event at the next QA meeting (GOV-07).
The Administrator audits a sample of homemaker and companion service records at least quarterly for compliance with duties and medication-reminder limits, and documents the results.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures homemaker and companion staff are trained on limits; monitors compliance; keeps registration or licensure current.
Screens each referral for hands-on needs and routes the client correctly.
Assesses clients whose needs change; writes the RN-supervised service plan for reassignment.
Perform only permitted duties; give verbal reminders only; document each visit; report new needs.

documentation: Homemaker/companion acknowledgment of limits (personnel file)
Service plan listing permitted duties (client record)
Written service record for every visit
RN reassessment note and updated plan when reassigned to an aide or CNA
Incident report and corrective action, if a violation occurs
Quarterly audit results

policies.title: Client Intake, Eligibility, Admission Criteria, Case Assignment and Assessment
policies.applies_to: Intake coordinator, scheduling staff, RN Supervisor and Administrator of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To set written criteria for accepting clients, assigning cases and managing cases, so that [AGENCY NAME] accepts only clients whose needs it can safely meet and assures every assigned visit.
policies.policy:
This policy meets Rule 59A-8.020(1), F.A.C. (Acceptance of Patients or Clients). [AGENCY NAME] accepts a client only when there is a reasonable expectation that services can be provided safely in the client's residence. This includes the ability to communicate with the client or the client's designee through a same-language staff person, an interpreter or translation technology (see CR-06). The agency assures that the client receives the services in the service plan or written agreement, including every assigned visit.

This policy meets Rule 59A-8.0095(2)(c)4, F.A.C. (Admission, Case Assignment and Case Management Policies and Records). The criteria for admission, case assignment and case management are set out in this policy, and the agency keeps records of how they were applied.

This policy meets Rule 59A-8.025(9), F.A.C. (Acceptance of Homemaker and Companion Clients). Before accepting a homemaker or companion client, the agency obtains all service-delivery information needed, determines that the services can be provided adequately and safely in the residence, and supplies employees or independent contractors capable of delivering the contracted services, including all visits.

Admission criteria: (a) the client needs only non-skilled services within the agency's license; (b) the agency has qualified staff available for the requested days and hours; (c) the home environment is reasonably safe for staff; (d) the agency can communicate with the client; and (e) the client or representative agrees to the written agreement and service plan. Clients whose needs exceed the non-skilled license, such as those needing skilled nursing, are declined or referred (see SVC-14).

definitions.definition: The process of receiving a referral, gathering information and deciding whether the agency can safely accept the client.
Selecting the specific aide, CNA, homemaker or companion for a client based on qualifications, availability, client needs and preferences.
The agency's ongoing coordination of a client's service plan, supervision, scheduling and communication with the client, family and payers.
Communication with the client through staff who speak the client's language, an interpreter or translation technology.

procedures: The intake coordinator records each referral on the day it is received: referral source, client name and contact information, requested services, days and hours, payer and any urgency.

The intake coordinator gathers the information needed to deliver services: the disability or health basis for the request, diet restrictions, allergies, activity limits, mobility and equipment needs, cognitive status, home environment, pets, emergency contacts and the client's language and communication needs.

The intake coordinator screens the referral against the admission criteria in this policy. If the client needs skilled nursing or any service outside the non-skilled license, the intake coordinator refers the case to the RN Supervisor to decline or refer under SVC-14 and gives the client or referral source other provider options.
The intake coordinator confirms how communication will occur: a same-language staff person, an interpreter or translation technology (CR-06), and documents the method on the intake form.

Scheduling staff confirm that qualified staff are available for every requested visit before acceptance. If the agency cannot assure all visits, the agency does not accept the client and refers the client elsewhere.

The RN Supervisor reviews the intake information for every client who needs hands-on care and conducts an initial assessment in the home, with the client's written consent for the RN to enter the home (SVC-06). The RN determines whether safe care is possible and what aide assignments are needed.
For homemaker and companion clients, the intake coordinator or RN Supervisor confirms that no hands-on care is needed (SVC-02) and that the services can be provided adequately and safely.

The Administrator approves or denies each admission decision within [NUMBER OF BUSINESS DAYS] business days of receiving a complete referral, and tells the client or referral source of the decision and, for a denial, the reason.

Scheduling staff assign cases by matching caregiver qualifications and training (PER-01, PER-04), the client's needs and preferences, language, geographic proximity and availability. The RN Supervisor confirms that each aide or CNA is qualified for the assignment (SVC-05).

Before services begin, the client or representative and an agency representative sign and date the written agreement, a copy goes to the client, and the original is placed in the client record (CR-07, SVC-04). Required notices are given at the start of service (CR-03), along with rights (CR-01) and emergency preparedness information (SAF-07).
The RN Supervisor or intake coordinator opens the client record (REC-01 or REC-02) containing the intake form, assessment, consent, agreement, service plan and assignment sheet.

The RN Supervisor and scheduling staff review each active case at least [NUMBER OF DAYS] days after start of service and whenever a change in condition is reported, to confirm the criteria are still met and that all visits are being covered. If criteria are no longer met, the RN Supervisor begins the process in SVC-12.

The intake coordinator keeps a log of all referrals, including those declined or referred, with the date, decision and reason, and the Administrator reviews the log quarterly as part of Quality Assurance (GOV-07).

responsibilities.duty: Receives referrals; gathers intake information; screens against criteria; maintains referral log.
Assesses clients needing hands-on care; confirms safe care is possible; confirms caregiver qualifications for assignments.
Confirm staff availability for all visits; assign cases; report coverage gaps immediately.
Approves or denies admissions; reviews records of criteria applied; ensures the agency does not overcommit.

documentation: Referral and intake form (including disability basis, diet restrictions, allergies, activity limits and language/communication method)
RN initial assessment (aide clients)
Written consent for the RN to enter the home
Admission decision, with reason for any denial or referral
Signed written agreement and service plan
Case assignment record and assignment sheet
Referral log of accepted, declined and referred clients

policies.title: Service Plan (Service Provision Plan) and Plan Updates
policies.applies_to: RN Supervisor, intake coordinator, scheduling staff, aides, CNAs, homemakers and companions of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure every client has a written service plan that states the services, rates and payment source, is shared with the client, and is kept current as the client's needs change.
policies.policy:
This policy meets Rule 59A-8.020(3), F.A.C. (Service Provision Plan). For homemaker and companion clients, and for home health aide clients who do not need a practitioner's treatment order, the signed, dated written agreement serves as the service provision plan under s. 400.491(2), F.S. The agreement is signed by an agency representative and the client or the client's representative, a copy is given to the client, and the original is kept in the client record for one year after services end.

The written agreement states the services to be provided, the rates for privately paid services and the payment sources (s. 400.487, F.S.). The agency tells the client, caregiver or guardian that they may be informed of the plan, participate in developing it, and have a copy on request (Rule 59A-8.0215(3), F.A.C.; s. 400.487, F.S.).

The RN Supervisor reviews the plan at supervisory visits and whenever the client's condition changes. Each aide or CNA works from an individualized assignment sheet that reflects the plan. If a physician or APRN treatment order is added, or skilled services are requested, the agency follows SVC-14 before any such service is provided.

definitions.definition: For clients with no treatment order, the signed written agreement listing the services, rates and payment source.
The individualized, dated list of tasks for a specific caregiver and client, prepared or approved by the RN.
A guardian, health care surrogate, agent under power of attorney or other legally authorized person acting for the client.
A documented change to the plan reflecting a change in the client's condition, schedule, services or preferences.

procedures: Before the first visit, the RN Supervisor (for aide clients) or intake coordinator (for homemaker and companion clients) prepares the written agreement, listing each service, the days and hours, the tasks, the rate for privately paid services and each payment source.
The agency representative reviews the agreement with the client or representative in a language the client understands (CR-06), and both sign and date it.
The agency representative gives the client or representative a copy of the signed agreement the same day and places the original in the client record.

At the same time, the agency representative tells the client, caregiver or guardian orally and in writing that they may be informed of the plan, participate in developing it, and receive a copy of the plan on request. The notice is documented in the record.

The RN Supervisor prepares an individualized assignment sheet for every aide or CNA, consistent with the plan and with SVC-01 and SVC-05. Homemaker and companion assignment sheets list only permitted duties (SVC-02).
Scheduling staff give the assignment sheet to the caregiver before the first visit and ensure a copy is available in the home or through the agency's electronic system.
Caregivers follow the assignment sheet and report to the RN Supervisor if a task on it cannot be performed safely or if the client's needs differ from the plan.
The RN Supervisor reviews the plan at every supervisory visit (SVC-06) and documents whether it still meets the client's needs.

When a client's condition or needs change (SVC-11), the RN Supervisor reassesses the client within [NUMBER OF BUSINESS DAYS] business days of the report, or sooner if there is a safety concern, and revises the plan and assignment sheet.

When the client requests a change in services, schedule or caregiver, the intake coordinator or RN Supervisor documents the request, discusses it with the client, and updates the plan. Rate or payment-source changes require a new or amended agreement signed and dated by both parties.
The RN Supervisor sends the revised assignment sheet to the caregiver and scheduling staff before the first visit under the revised plan, and confirms the caregiver understands the change.
If a physician or APRN treatment order exists or skilled services are requested, the RN Supervisor follows SVC-14 and does not begin those services under this policy.
The agency keeps each service provision plan for one year after services end, or longer if the retention period in REC-01 is longer.

responsibilities.duty: Prepares and revises plans for aide clients; reviews plans at supervisory visits and on changes in condition; prepares assignment sheets.
Prepares agreements for homemaker and companion clients; gives the client notice of the right to participate and obtain a copy.
Follow the assignment sheet; report changes or tasks that cannot be performed.
Audits plans for completeness and timely updates.

documentation: Signed and dated written agreement / service provision plan (original in record, copy to client)
Documentation of notice of right to be informed of, participate in and receive a copy of the plan
Assignment sheets and revisions
RN plan review notes and reassessments
Records of requested changes and amended agreements

policies.title: Delegation and RN Assignment of Personal Care Tasks
policies.applies_to: RN Supervisor, aides, CNAs, scheduling staff and the Administrator of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To set how the RN assigns and delegates personal care tasks, confirms that each aide or CNA is qualified for each assignment, and keeps full responsibility for those tasks.
policies.policy:
This policy meets Rule 59A-8.0095(3)(b), F.A.C. (RN Assignment of Personal Care Tasks). An RN may assign personal care tasks to LPNs, CNAs and home health aides. The RN keeps full responsibility for those tasks and ensures that each aide or CNA is qualified for each assignment based on training and experience.

This policy meets Rule 59A-8.0095(2)(c)5, F.A.C. (Delegation Policies and Procedures). The agency adopts the written delegation procedures below for nursing tasks and activities as specified in Chapter 64B9-14, F.A.C. The RN follows Chapter 64B9-14 whenever delegating any nursing task.

Because [AGENCY NAME] provides only non-skilled services, it does not employ LPNs to provide skilled care and does not assign skilled nursing tasks to unlicensed staff. Any request to add skilled services or LPNs is handled under SVC-14. All assignments stay within SVC-01.

definitions.definition: The RN's direction that a qualified aide or CNA perform specific personal care tasks for a specific client.
The transfer by a licensed nurse of the authority to perform a nursing task to another person, in accordance with Chapter 64B9-14, F.A.C.
The aide or CNA has the required certification or training, has demonstrated the tasks, and has the experience needed to perform them safely for the particular client.
The registered nurse designated by the agency to assign tasks, supervise aides and CNAs, and make supervisory visits.

procedures: The Administrator designates in writing at least one RN with a current, unencumbered Florida license, or a compact license valid in Florida, as RN Supervisor and keeps the designation in the agency's administrative file.
Before assigning any task, the RN Supervisor reviews the client's assessment, service plan and risk factors (SVC-03, SVC-04), and identifies the personal care tasks the client needs.

The RN Supervisor reviews each candidate caregiver's personnel file (PER-07) for current CNA certification or the 40-hour training or passed competency test, the 2-hour medication-assistance training, orientation and competency evaluation (PER-04), and relevant experience.

The RN Supervisor decides whether the caregiver is qualified for each task. If a task needs client-specific teaching, the RN Supervisor teaches it and observes a return demonstration before the caregiver performs it alone, and documents this.

The RN Supervisor issues a written, dated assignment sheet that lists only the tasks assigned to that caregiver for that client. The assignment sheet is placed in the client file and given to the caregiver.

For any task that qualifies as a nursing task delegation, the RN follows the written delegation criteria in Chapter 64B9-14, F.A.C., and documents the delegation, the competency verification and the instructions given. The RN does not delegate any task prohibited by SVC-01.

The RN Supervisor does not assign tasks to a caregiver who lacks the required qualifications, and tells scheduling staff to assign a different caregiver. Scheduling staff do not assign a caregiver to a case until the RN Supervisor has approved the assignment.

The caregiver confirms understanding of the assignment, performs only the assigned tasks, and reports to the RN Supervisor any task that cannot be done safely, any change in the client and any request for additional tasks.

The RN Supervisor reviews assignments at each supervisory visit (SVC-06), when the client's condition changes (SVC-11) and when a different caregiver is assigned. The RN revises or ends assignments as needed and documents the change.
If an assigned caregiver performs a task outside the assignment, the RN Supervisor addresses it under SVC-01, retrains the caregiver and notifies the Administrator.
The Administrator reviews a sample of assignment sheets at least quarterly for completeness and for consistency with caregiver qualifications and records the results for Quality Assurance (GOV-07).
The agency does not assign personal care tasks to an LPN unless skilled services have been properly added under SVC-14.

responsibilities.duty: Assigns and delegates tasks; verifies caregiver qualifications; remains fully responsible for the assigned tasks; documents assignments.
Designates the RN Supervisor; ensures delegation procedures are followed; audits assignments.
Accept only assignments they are trained to perform; perform tasks as assigned; report concerns.
Assign only caregivers approved by the RN Supervisor.

documentation: RN Supervisor designation
Written assignment sheets for each caregiver and client
Client-specific teaching and return-demonstration records
Delegation documentation under Chapter 64B9-14, F.A.C.
Quarterly assignment audit results

policies.title: Supervision of Caregivers and RN Supervisory Visits
policies.applies_to: RN Supervisor, aides, CNAs, clients and representatives, and the Administrator of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To provide RN supervision of aides and CNAs in the home, with the client's consent, based on the client's condition and the caregiver's training and experience, and to document each supervisory visit.
policies.policy:
This policy meets Rule 59A-8.0095(3)(c)-(d), F.A.C. (RN Supervisory Visits and On-Site Supervision). The agency arranges RN supervisory visits to the home of a client receiving aide services, according to the client's direction, approval and agreement to pay for the visits (s. 400.487, F.S.). The agency obtains written consent from the client or the client's guardian or legal representative for the RN to enter the home. The RN provides on-site supervision as needed, based on the severity of the client's condition and the aide's or CNA's training and experience. The rule sets no fixed frequency, so the RN determines and documents the frequency for each client. Every supervisory visit is documented in the client file.

Supervisory-visit notes are part of the required client record (see REC-01). Because the agency provides no skilled care, it has no director of nursing; the RN Supervisor performs these supervisory functions.

definitions.definition: An RN visit to the client's home to observe and evaluate the aide or CNA, review the service plan, and check the client's status and satisfaction.
RN supervision in the home, provided as needed based on the client's condition and the caregiver's training and experience.

definitions.term: Written consent to enter the home
definitions.definition: A signed statement by the client or the client's guardian or legal representative authorizing the RN to enter the home for supervision.

procedures: At admission, the RN Supervisor or intake coordinator explains RN supervisory visits to the client or representative, including their purpose, that visits are arranged according to the client's direction and approval, and any charges for them.

The client or representative signs a written consent for the RN to enter the home and for any agreed charge for supervisory visits (CR-07). The agency does not send an RN into the home without this written consent. The consent is filed in the client record.

The RN Supervisor sets the frequency and type of supervision for each client based on the severity of the client's condition, the tasks assigned, the aide's or CNA's training and experience, and any complaints or incidents, and records the reasons in the client file.

The RN Supervisor makes the first supervisory visit as set in the plan and observes the caregiver performing the assigned tasks whenever possible. A newly hired caregiver, or a caregiver newly assigned to a client with complex needs, receives closer supervision than an experienced caregiver on a stable assignment.

During each supervisory visit, the RN Supervisor observes the caregiver's performance and compliance with the assignment sheet, reviews the visit records, checks the client's condition and safety, asks the client about satisfaction and any concerns, and reviews medication-assistance practices (SVC-08).
For a client whose condition is medically stable, the RN Supervisor reviews the client's status as required by Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(m) and documents the review in the record.
The RN Supervisor reviews the service plan at every visit and updates the plan and assignment sheet if needed (SVC-04, SVC-05).

The RN Supervisor documents each visit in the client file on the same day or the next business day: date, time, persons present, observations, findings, teaching given, changes to the plan and follow-up actions.

If the RN Supervisor finds unsafe or incompetent practice, the RN corrects it on the spot, retrains the caregiver, notifies the Administrator the same day, and increases supervision as appropriate. If the client is in danger, the RN follows SVC-11 and SAF-01 as needed.

If the client declines supervisory visits or refuses to pay for them, the RN Supervisor explains the purpose, documents the informed decision, and offers alternatives such as phone check-ins with the client and caregiver. The RN Supervisor evaluates whether services can be provided safely without visits and consults with the Administrator; if not, the agency begins SVC-12.

The RN Supervisor is available to caregivers by phone during all hours of client service (SVC-07) and may make an unscheduled on-site visit at any time that the condition of the client or the performance of the caregiver requires it.

The Administrator reviews supervisory-visit records for each active client at least quarterly, verifies that the visit frequency is consistent with the documented reasons, and reports findings to the Quality Assurance process (GOV-07).

responsibilities.duty: Determines supervision frequency; makes and documents visits; corrects practice; reviews and updates plans.
Ensures an RN is available; audits supervisory-visit records; resolves refusal of supervision.
Cooperate with supervision; follow RN direction; report concerns.
Directs and approves supervisory visits; signs the consent to enter the home; agrees to any charges.

documentation: Signed consent for the RN to enter the home
Agreement to pay, if any, for supervisory visits (service agreement)
RN note on supervision frequency and reasons
Supervisory-visit notes for every visit
Documentation of any client refusal of visits and alternatives offered
Corrective-action and retraining records
Quarterly audit results

policies.title: Availability of the RN Supervisor During Hours of Client Service
policies.applies_to: Registered nurse supervisor and backup RN, home health aides, CNAs, scheduling staff, Administrator, and all clients receiving hands-on aide services from [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure a registered nurse supervisor can be reached by aides and clients during every hour that [AGENCY NAME] provides client service, so that changes in condition, delegation questions and supervision needs are answered promptly.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] provides non-skilled services only and has no director of nursing. It therefore has written policies on the availability of a registered nurse (RN) supervisor during hours of client service. This policy meets Rule 59A-8.003(9)(d), F.A.C. (official checklist item 59A-8.003(9)(d)-2: written policies and procedures on the availability of a registered nurse supervisor during hours of patient service, applicable to a non-skilled personal care agency). An RN is designated as supervisor and a backup RN is designated for every hour in which any aide or CNA is in a client's home. A telephone number staffed by or forwarded to the on-duty RN is published to all aides and clients. The RN may assign personal care tasks and remains fully responsible for them, provides supervisory visits with the client's written consent to enter the home, and arranges on-site supervision as needed based on the severity of the client's condition and the aide's training and experience, documented in the client file (Rule 59A-8.0095). This policy is separate from the Administrator's weekday public-availability requirement in GOV-02.

definitions.definition: The Florida-licensed registered nurse designated by [AGENCY NAME] to supervise aides and CNAs, accept their reports and make supervisory visits.
A second Florida-licensed registered nurse designated to cover when the RN supervisor is unavailable.
Every hour, including nights, weekends and holidays, when an aide, CNA, homemaker or companion employed or contracted by [AGENCY NAME] is scheduled to be in a client's home.
The published telephone number, [PHONE], that reaches the on-duty RN supervisor or backup RN during all hours of client service.
A call about a change in client condition, injury, fall, refusal of care, medication concern, safety threat or any situation the aide cannot resolve under the service plan.

procedures: The Administrator, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME], designates in writing the RN supervisor, [RN SUPERVISOR NAME], and at least one backup RN, [BACKUP RN NAME], and confirms each holds a current Florida RN license before the designation takes effect.

Before the start of each scheduling period, the scheduler prepares an RN coverage schedule that lists the on-duty RN supervisor and backup RN for every hour in which client service is scheduled. The schedule is approved by the Administrator and kept on file.

Before any hour of client service is scheduled, the scheduler checks that an RN is named on the coverage schedule for that hour. If no RN is covered, the Administrator arranges coverage or the visit is not scheduled.

The supervisory line [PHONE] is staffed by the on-duty RN or forwarded to the RN's mobile phone. The number is printed on every aide's ID badge or care-plan sheet, on the client's service agreement packet and in the client's home copy of the service plan.

At hire and at orientation, each aide and CNA is told how to reach the RN supervisor, which situations require a call (see steps 7-8), and that the RN backup is called if the first RN does not answer within 10 minutes.

The on-duty RN keeps the supervisory line available and returns calls as follows: urgent calls are answered immediately or returned within 15 minutes; routine calls are returned within 1 hour during service hours.

Aides and CNAs call the RN supervisor immediately for any change in the client's condition, including changes in appearance or behavior, new injury, fall, refusal of care, medication concern, or a task they have not been trained or delegated to do. Aides call 911 first for a life-threatening emergency and then notify the RN (see SVC-11).
Aides and CNAs call the RN supervisor, or the RN for the shift, before performing any task that is not on the service plan and before accepting a client's request to change tasks.

The RN gives instructions, decides whether the plan needs updating or an RN visit is needed, and tells the aide what to do. The RN can order an on-site visit and arrange for one, within the limits of the client's written consent to RN entry into the home.

If the RN decides on-site supervision is needed, the RN schedules the visit based on the severity of the client's condition and the aide's training and experience, and documents the reason in the client file (see SVC-06).

If the RN cannot be reached by phone within 15 minutes for an urgent call, the aide calls the backup RN, then the Administrator or alternate. The aide must not wait for a call back if the client is in danger.
The RN logs every contact on the RN Contact Log immediately after the call: date, time, caller, client, reason, advice given, follow-up and time the RN responded.
The RN places any care-related instruction in the client record and updates the service plan or delegation when needed (see SVC-04 and SVC-05).
If an RN must leave coverage mid-shift or becomes unavailable, the RN notifies the backup RN and the Administrator and the supervisory line is forwarded before the RN leaves.

Each month the Administrator reviews the RN Contact Log and coverage schedule against the schedule of client service hours to confirm coverage was continuous and call returns met the stated times. Gaps and late returns are corrective-action items in QA (see GOV-07).
The Administrator reviews this policy at least annually and whenever service hours, RN staff or the supervisory phone number changes.

responsibilities.duty: Designates the RN supervisor and backup, approves the RN coverage schedule, ensures coverage for every service hour and reviews logs monthly.
Answer the supervisory line, return calls within stated times, give instructions, document contacts, and arrange supervisory or on-site visits.
Does not schedule client service for any hour without named RN coverage and distributes the supervisory number.
Call the RN promptly for changes in condition and for questions about tasks, and follow the RN's instructions.

documentation: RN coverage schedule by service hours
RN Contact Log
Written designation of RN supervisor and backup RN, with license verification
Client file entries for RN instructions and on-site supervision decisions
Monthly coverage review notes and QA minutes

policies.title: Medication Assistance and Self-Administration Support
policies.applies_to: Home health aides, CNAs, RN supervisor, intake staff and clients who request help with self-administered medication; does not apply to homemaker and companion staff, who provide no hands-on care
policies.purpose: To allow only safe, lawful, limited unlicensed help with medications a client takes for themself, and to prevent aides from administering medication or exercising clinical judgment.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] allows aides and CNAs to assist with self-administration of medication only as permitted by s. 400.488, F.S. and Rule 59A-8.0095, F.A.C. Assistance is given only to a medically stable client, with routine, regularly scheduled medications, upon a documented request and the client's written informed consent. This policy meets Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(m)-(o), F.A.C. (official checklist item 59A-8.0095(5)(m)-(o)). Under (5)(m), an RN reviews and reconciles all prescribed and over-the-counter medications to confirm the client is medically stable with routine scheduled medications. Under (5)(n), a licensed health care professional informs the client or caregiver of the arrangement and obtains written consent under s. 400.488(2). Under (5)(o)1-4, aides may take only the actions permitted by rule, which are described in this policy; any other action is prohibited. Aides complete 2 hours of medication-assistance training, including a check that they can read the prescription label, before they provide this help (Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(c)15).

definitions.definition: Limited help given to a client who takes their own medication, as listed in s. 400.488(3) and Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(o). It is not administration of medication.
A condition that does not require nursing assessment or judgment to determine dose, timing or response to medication, as confirmed by RN review.
A medication taken on a set schedule, with fixed dose and time. It does not include a medication taken as needed that requires judgment.
The RN's review of all prescribed and over-the-counter medications the client takes, compared with the prescriber's orders and pharmacy labels.
A written record of each assist given by the aide, kept in the client record as required by s. 400.488(3).

procedures: At intake or when a client asks for medication help, the intake coordinator documents the request in the client record, including who made it and the date, and refers the client to the RN supervisor.

The RN reviews and reconciles all prescribed and over-the-counter medications the client takes, using the labeled containers, pharmacy list or prescriber orders, and records the review in the client record (Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(m)).

The RN decides whether the client is medically stable with routine, regularly scheduled medications. If the client is not medically stable or any medication is excluded (see step 9), the RN documents that aide assistance will not be provided and informs the client or caregiver.

If the client qualifies, a licensed health care professional (the RN or the client's licensed provider) informs the client or caregiver of the arrangement, explains what the aide will and will not do, and obtains the client's signed written informed consent under s. 400.488(2) (Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(n)).
The signed consent and the RN reconciliation are placed in the client record before any assistance starts. A copy of the consent is given to the client.

Only aides whose training records show the 2-hour medication-assistance course and a passed label-reading check may help with medications. The scheduler assigns only those aides to clients with medication assistance on the service plan.
The medication-assistance task and its schedule are written into the service plan (SVC-04) and, where an RN assigns it, into the RN's delegation (SVC-05).

At each assist, the aide permitted actions are limited to those allowed by s. 400.488(3) and Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(o)1-4: bringing the client's properly labeled, previously dispensed medication from where it is stored, reading the label with the client, opening the container, helping with removing the prescribed amount in the client's presence, helping the client with taking it, and returning the container to proper storage.

Aides must not: give or help with injectables; administer through any tube; mix or calculate doses or change a dose; give any as-needed (PRN) medication that requires judgment about whether or when to give it; or give rectal, urethral or vaginal preparations (s. 400.488(4)). Aides must not decide to withhold, add, substitute or change any medication.

After each assist, the aide records on the medication assist record the date, time, medication name, dose as labeled and any refusal, and signs it (s. 400.488(3)). The aide never records an assist that did not happen.

If the label cannot be read, does not match the client's list, the container is damaged, the client refuses, or the client seems ill or confused, the aide does not assist and calls the RN supervisor immediately (SVC-07). The aide records the event.

Other tasks allowed by s. 400.488(6) are limited as follows and only when delegated by the RN and written into the service plan: use of a glucometer; applying antiembolism stockings; placing an oxygen cannula, with no titration or change of flow rate; placing a CPAP, with no titration; taking vital signs; and emptying or changing colostomy bags. The aide reports readings and any concern to the RN.

If the client's condition or medications change, including a new prescription, hospital stay or new symptom, the aide stops assisting with the changed medication and informs the RN, who repeats the review and, if needed, new consent before assistance resumes.

The RN reviews medication assist records during each supervisory visit and compares them with labels and the service plan. Discrepancies are investigated and recorded; medication errors are reported on an incident report (SAF-02).
The Administrator reviews medication assist records and errors in QA each quarter (GOV-07). Training records are checked annually at in-service (PER-04).

responsibilities.duty: Reviews and reconciles medications, determines medical stability, delegates tasks and reviews records during supervisory visits.
Informs the client or caregiver and obtains written consent under s. 400.488(2).
Provide only permitted assistance, keep the record of each assist, refuse excluded actions and report concerns to the RN.
Assigns only aides with documented medication-assistance training.
Ensures consents, training and records are in place and reviews errors in QA.

documentation: Client's documented request for medication assistance
RN medication review and reconciliation
Client's signed written informed consent
Medication assist record for each assist
Aide training record showing 2-hour medication-assistance course and label-reading check
Incident reports for medication errors

policies.title: Scheduling, Missed Visits and Continuity of Care
policies.applies_to: Scheduling staff, aides, CNAs, homemakers, companions, RN supervisor, Administrator and all clients served by [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure every client receives all of the visits assigned to them, and that missed or late visits are reported, covered and reviewed.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] accepts a client only when it can reasonably provide the visits safely and it assures the client all assigned visits are made (Rule 59A-8.020(1), F.A.C.). For clients served under the homemaker and companion registration, the agency accepts the client only if services can be provided adequately and safely, and it supplies capable staff for all visits (Rule 59A-8.025(9), F.A.C.). Each case has an assigned primary caregiver and a named backup. Missed and late visits are reported at once to the client and RN supervisor, covered whenever possible, logged and reviewed in quality assurance. Travel time between clients is paid work time and is handled under PER-08.

definitions.definition: A visit on the service plan or service agreement with a date, start time and duration.
An assigned visit that is not made, or made more than 2 hours late, without the client's agreement.
A visit that starts more than 30 minutes after the scheduled time.
A trained, qualified caregiver named for the case who can cover when the primary caregiver cannot.
A visit provided at a different time to replace a missed visit, with the client's agreement.

procedures: Before accepting a client, the intake coordinator and scheduler confirm that qualified staff are available for every visit on the proposed schedule (SVC-03). If not, the client is told and referred elsewhere rather than accepted.

The scheduler assigns a primary caregiver and names a backup caregiver for each case on the schedule, matching training, delegated tasks and language needs. Aides with medication-assistance tasks must have the required training (SVC-08).
The scheduler gives each client and caregiver the schedule in writing before service starts and when it changes, and posts the supervisory number [PHONE] on it.

Caregivers who cannot make a visit, or expect to be more than 30 minutes late, must call the scheduler as early as possible, and at least 4 hours before the visit whenever the reason is known in advance.
The scheduler immediately assigns the backup caregiver or another qualified caregiver. The client is called at once with the name of the replacement or new arrival time.

If no replacement can be found, the scheduler calls the client or representative, offers a make-up visit, and notifies the RN supervisor the same day. The RN decides whether a gap in service creates a risk and arranges other contacts, such as a family member or the client's care coordinator.

For clients who live alone or are at high risk (for example, those who need help with eating, toileting or medications), the RN supervisor or Administrator is called before the scheduler leaves the case uncovered, and a safety check is arranged.

If a caregiver does not arrive and has not called, the scheduler tries the caregiver by phone within 15 minutes of the scheduled start, calls the client, sends a replacement, and reports the event to the Administrator.
The scheduler enters every missed or late visit in the Missed Visit Log: date, client, caregiver, scheduled time, reason, who was notified and when, and the make-up plan.

For Medicaid or other third-party funded clients, the scheduler also notifies the payer or care coordinator when that payer requires notice of missed visits (SVC-13), and documents EVV corrections (SVC-10).
The Administrator reviews the Missed Visit Log weekly, counseling caregivers for avoidable misses and fixing scheduling problems, such as too few backup staff.
Each quarter, the QA committee reviews the Missed Visit Log for missed-visit rates, repeated causes, clients most often affected and staffing needs, and records actions taken (GOV-07).
Clients may report missed or late visits through the complaint process, and complaints are logged under CR-02.

If staffing falls so that the agency cannot assure all assigned visits, the Administrator stops accepting new clients and, if needed, works with the RN supervisor to refer clients to other providers following SVC-12.

responsibilities.duty: Assigns primary and backup caregivers, sends schedules, covers missed visits, notifies clients and the RN, and logs each event.
Arrive on time, call early when unable to attend and never leave a client without notice.
Assesses risk from a service gap and arranges safety follow-up.
Reviews logs weekly, assures sufficient staff and chairs the QA review.

documentation: Client and caregiver schedules
Backup caregiver designation in case file
Missed Visit Log
Notices to clients and payers
QA minutes showing review of missed visits

policies.title: Electronic Visit Verification and Timekeeping
policies.applies_to: Aides, CNAs, homemakers, companions, schedulers, billing and payroll staff, and the Administrator
policies.purpose: To verify each visit electronically where required, record actual hours worked accurately, and make sure billing and wages match the visits actually provided.
policies.policy: Electronic visit verification (EVV) is required for Medicaid personal care services (from January 1, 2020) and Medicaid home health care services (from January 1, 2023) under 42 U.S.C. 1396b(l). [AGENCY NAME] uses the EVV system each Statewide Medicaid Managed Care (SMMC) Long-Term Care plan or the Agency for Persons with Disabilities (APD) requires, and records actual start and stop times for all visits, including private-pay visits. As a third-party employer, [AGENCY NAME] may not claim the federal companionship or live-in exemptions, so overtime applies and all hours worked are recorded (29 CFR 552.109). Wages paid must meet the Florida minimum wage, which is $15.00 per hour from September 30, 2026, and no local rate higher than the state's private-sector minimum applies (Fla. Const. Art. X, s. 24; s. 448.110, F.S.; s. 218.077, F.S.).

definitions.definition: A system that electronically records the type of service, the client, the caregiver, the date and the actual start and end times and location of a visit.
The time the caregiver actually begins and ends service, as recorded by the caregiver in the EVV system.
A change to a recorded visit made with a documented reason and approval.
All time a caregiver works for [AGENCY NAME], including visit time and required travel between clients, as defined under PER-08.

procedures: The Administrator identifies, for each payer (each SMMC LTC plan, APD, Area Agency on Aging contract), the EVV system and rules that apply, and records them in the payer file (SVC-13).
Billing staff set up each client and authorization in the required EVV system before the first visit, and the scheduler enters the schedule to match the service plan.
At orientation, caregivers are trained to use the EVV application or telephone system, to clock in on arrival and clock out on departure at the client's home, and not to clock for another person.

Caregivers clock in and out at the start and end of each visit using the actual time. Caregivers must not clock in early, clock out late or clock in from outside the client's home unless the system allows it for a documented reason.

If the system fails or the client has no phone or signal, the caregiver calls the scheduler, writes the actual times on a paper timesheet signed by the client or representative, and the office enters the visit with the reason noted.

The scheduler reviews EVV exceptions each day: missed clock-ins, late arrivals, short visits, overlapping visits and out-of-location visits. Exceptions are resolved with the caregiver the same or next business day.

A correction to a recorded time is made only by the scheduler or a designated supervisor with the reason recorded (for example, forgot to clock out), the caregiver's confirmation and the person's name and date. Corrections are never made to inflate hours or to bill for care not given.
Billing staff reconcile EVV records to the service plan, authorization, payroll and the claim before each claim is submitted. Visits that do not match are held and investigated (GOV-08).

Payroll staff pay caregivers for actual hours recorded, including overtime at the required rate for hours over 40 in a workweek and required travel time between clients (PER-08). Pay rates are checked against the Florida minimum wage when it changes, including the $15.00 rate effective September 30, 2026.
Payroll staff do not apply the federal companionship or live-in exemptions to any caregiver employed by [AGENCY NAME].
Each month, the Administrator reviews EVV-to-payroll-to-billing reconciliation and the count of manual corrections. Patterns of corrections by a caregiver or scheduler are investigated and corrected.

Each quarter, the QA committee reviews EVV exceptions and corrections (GOV-07). Suspected falsification of times is reported to the Administrator, handled under GOV-08 and PER-09, and may lead to discipline up to termination.
EVV, timesheet and correction records are kept with billing and payroll records for the period required in REC-01.

responsibilities.duty: Clock in and out accurately in real time and report system problems.
Sets up schedules, reviews exceptions daily and approves corrections with a documented reason.
Set up EVV for each payer and reconcile EVV to claims.
Pay all hours worked, overtime and minimum wage, and reconcile to EVV.
Reviews monthly reconciliation and corrections and addresses falsification.

documentation: EVV system records and exception reports
Paper timesheets with client signature when used
EVV correction log with reasons and approvals
Payroll and billing reconciliation reports
Caregiver EVV training records
QA minutes

policies.title: Change in Client Condition and Emergencies in the Home
policies.applies_to: All aides, CNAs, homemakers, companions, the RN supervisor, scheduling staff and the Administrator
policies.purpose: To make sure caregivers recognize and report changes in a client's condition, respond correctly in emergencies, and follow the client's DNR order.
policies.policy: Aides observe and report to the RN supervisor changes in a client's appearance and gross behavior (Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(l)5, F.A.C.). Caregiver training covers recognition of emergencies and follow-up (Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(c), topic 7). In a life-threatening emergency, the caregiver calls 911 first. Personnel may withhold cardiopulmonary resuscitation only on a valid Florida Do Not Resuscitate Order (DNRO) under s. 401.45, F.S. (s. 400.487(7), F.S.). Aides and CNAs keep current CPR certification (Rule 59A-8.0095(5)(k)). Caregivers do not diagnose, give medical advice or decide treatment. The RN supervisor, emergency contact and physician are notified, and an incident report is completed (SAF-02).

definitions.definition: Any new or worsening sign, symptom, behavior, injury, fall, confusion, refusal of food, fluids or care, or safety concern different from the client's usual state.
A situation such as unresponsiveness, not breathing, chest pain, stroke signs, severe bleeding, choking, seizure that does not stop, or serious injury.
A valid Florida Do Not Resuscitate Order signed by the physician and client or representative on the state-prescribed form, under s. 401.45, F.S.
The person the client has named to be called in an emergency, recorded in the client record.

procedures: At admission, the RN records in the client record the client's usual condition, diagnoses reported, emergency contacts, physician, preferred hospital and whether a DNRO exists (SVC-03, CR-08). The caregiver is shown where to find this information in the home.
At orientation, and each year at in-service, caregivers are trained to recognize emergencies and changes in condition and follow up, and to hold current CPR certification (PER-04).

In a life-threatening emergency, the caregiver calls 911 first, gives the address and the client's condition, and stays with the client. The caregiver starts CPR or first aid within their training unless a valid DNRO is present and shown.

If a DNRO is present, the caregiver confirms it is the valid state form, signed and on hand, withholds CPR in accordance with it, and still calls 911 and the RN. If the caregiver cannot confirm that the DNRO is valid, the caregiver follows the 911 operator's instructions.
After calling 911, the caregiver immediately calls the supervisory line [PHONE] to reach the RN supervisor (SVC-07), then the emergency contact. The RN notifies the physician when appropriate.

For a non-emergency change in condition (for example, new confusion, a fall without apparent injury, skin changes, refusal of meals or medication, unusual behavior), the caregiver does not wait until the next visit; the caregiver calls the RN supervisor during the same visit and follows the RN's instructions.
The RN assesses the report by phone, decides whether to advise a call to the physician, call 911, arrange an RN visit or change the service plan, and documents the decision in the client record.
Caregivers do not move an injured client unless the client is in immediate danger, do not give medications other than those permitted under SVC-08, and do not give medical advice.
If the caregiver is in danger or the client has a weapon or violent family member is present, the caregiver leaves, calls 911 and the RN supervisor, and follows SAF-08.

If a client dies, the caregiver calls 911 (unless a hospice or valid DNRO instructions apply), then the RN supervisor and emergency contact, and does not disturb the scene beyond what emergency personnel direct.

If the client is taken to the hospital, the caregiver gives the responders the medication list and emergency contact information from the client's file, and informs the scheduler so that visits are held or changed.
The caregiver completes a written incident report the same day and the RN completes the follow-up (SAF-02). Suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation is reported under SAF-01 immediately.
The RN updates the service plan after the event if care needs have changed (SVC-04) and informs the payer or care coordinator when required (SVC-13).
The Administrator reviews emergency events in QA each quarter for trends and training needs (GOV-07).

responsibilities.duty: Observe and report changes, call 911 first in life-threatening emergencies, follow a valid DNRO, call the RN and document the event.
Assesses reports, decides on follow-up, notifies the physician and updates the service plan.
Adjusts visits after an emergency and notifies the RN and Administrator.
Ensures CPR and emergency training and reviews events in QA.

documentation: Incident report
RN notes on each report of change in condition
Copy of valid DNRO in client record, when present
Emergency contact and physician information
Caregiver CPR certification and emergency-training records
QA minutes

policies.title: Discharge, Transfer and Termination of Services
policies.applies_to: Administrator, RN supervisor, intake and scheduling staff, case managers and all clients of [AGENCY NAME], including those served under the homemaker and companion registration
policies.purpose: To make sure that when services end, clients who need continuing care are not left without a plan, receive written notice of the date and reason, and are helped to find other providers or public programs.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] terminates services only for stated reasons and follows a written termination process. This policy meets Rule 59A-8.020(4), F.A.C. (official checklist item 59A-8.020(4)). For a client who needs continuing care, [AGENCY NAME] develops a plan and refers the client to another agency or provider before termination. The client is given written notice of the termination date, the reason (s. 400.491, F.S.) and the plan for continued services. This does not apply to private-pay clients who default through non-payment. If private funds are depleted, [AGENCY NAME] helps the client assess eligibility for government-funded programs (the social work assistance in the rule). A copy of the written termination notice is placed in the record, as is required of homemaker and companion registrants in Rule 59A-8.025(8)(h), F.A.C., and a termination summary is placed in the client record under REC-01 and REC-02.

definitions.definition: Ending services by [AGENCY NAME] for any reason, other than the client's own request or death.
The end of services because the service plan goals are met, services are no longer needed, the client dies, or the client or representative asks to stop.
Moving the client's care to another provider or agency, at the request of the client or by referral.
Care the client still needs for health and safety after [AGENCY NAME] stops services.
Non-payment by a client who pays privately for services under the service agreement (CR-07).

procedures: Services end only for one of these reasons: the client or representative asks to stop; the client's needs can no longer be met safely by the agency; services are no longer needed; the client is admitted to a facility or moves out of the service area; the client dies; non-payment by a private-pay client; or serious safety risk to staff or repeated refusal to follow the agreed plan. The reason is recorded.

Before any termination by the agency, the RN supervisor and the Administrator review the case and confirm the reason, the client's continuing care needs and available alternatives. The decision is recorded in the client record.

For a client who needs continuing care, the RN or case manager develops a written transition plan that lists the client's needs, the receiving provider or agency, and how the transfer will happen, and makes the referral before termination takes effect.

The agency gives the client or representative written notice that states the termination date, the reason and the plan for continued services, and lists the referral made. Unless there is immediate danger to the client or staff, notice is given at least 14 days before the date of termination.

If a safety risk requires faster action, the Administrator may end service immediately, but still gives the written notice and referral as soon as possible and informs the client's emergency contact and, when required, the payer.
The notice is delivered by hand or mail, and the delivery date and method are documented. A copy is placed in the client record.

The RN or case manager offers to help the client assess eligibility for government-funded programs if private funds are depleted, which includes referral to the Area Agency on Aging or Aging and Disability Resource Center, SMMC LTC, APD iBudget, or DCF for Medicaid eligibility, as appropriate (SVC-13).

For private-pay clients who default through non-payment, the agency follows the service agreement terms (CR-07). Written notice is still given, but a plan and referral are not required under the rule; the agency still tries to ensure the client's safety.
For Medicaid-funded clients, the agency notifies the plan care coordinator or payer, follows the payer's requirements for transition, and bills for no services after the end date.

If the client has been a victim or suspected victim of abuse, neglect or exploitation, the agency reports under SAF-01 and does not terminate without the RN and Administrator reviewing the safety of the client.
On the end date, the scheduler cancels the remaining visits and notifies the caregivers. The agency returns any client property, and the caregiver returns any keys (CR-05).

Within 7 days of the end date, the RN completes a termination summary that states the services provided, the client's condition at the end, the reason for ending, and the referral and plan, and places it in the client record with the notice.
For a client who requests discharge or when goals are met, the RN documents this, and the client or representative signs an acknowledgement when possible.

Records are kept as required (REC-01 and REC-02; the service agreement or service provision plan is kept for one year after termination under Rule 59A-8.020(3)). The Administrator reviews terminations quarterly in QA for patterns and for compliance with notice requirements (GOV-07).

responsibilities.duty: Approves each agency-initiated termination, ensures notice and referral and reviews terminations in QA.
Assesses continuing care needs, develops the transition plan, makes the referral and completes the termination summary.
Prepare and deliver the notice, cancel visits and notify caregivers and payers.
Stop billing as of the end date and handle private-pay balances under the service agreement.

documentation: Written termination notice with date, reason and plan for continued services
Transition plan and referral record
Record of help given on eligibility for government programs
Termination summary in client record
Notices to payers and care coordinators
QA minutes on terminations

policies.title: Coordination with Medicaid Programs and Payers (SMMC LTC, APD iBudget, Area Agencies on Aging)
policies.applies_to: Administrator, intake and scheduling staff, RN supervisor, billing staff, home health aides and CNAs, and personal supports staff serving clients whose services are paid by Medicaid or a public program
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] is properly enrolled and credentialed before it serves clients paid by Florida Medicaid or another public program, and that it follows each payer's authorization, billing, electronic visit verification (EVV) and reporting rules.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] accepts clients paid by Statewide Medicaid Managed Care Long-Term Care (SMMC LTC) plans, the Agency for Persons with Disabilities (APD) iBudget Florida waiver, and Area Agencies on Aging (AAA) programs only after it has enrolled with or been credentialed by the payer and holds a service authorization for the client. The agency enrolls as a Florida Medicaid provider and then credentials with each SMMC LTC plan in the regions it serves, because network providers serving SMMC plans must be screened and enrolled with Florida Medicaid (42 CFR 438.602). State-plan personal care (billing code S9122) covers recipients under age 21 only (Rule 59G-4.215, F.A.C.). The agency therefore does not assume that state-plan rates apply to adult clients. Adult SMMC LTC rates are negotiated with each plan and are set out in the plan contract. The agency complies with federal EVV requirements for Medicaid personal care and home health services (42 U.S.C. 1396b(l)). It also supports the person-centered service planning and home and community-based setting expectations that apply to waiver and LTC services (42 CFR 441.301(c) and 42 CFR 441.710). Staff who provide APD iBudget Personal Supports meet the iBudget Waiver Coverage and Limitations Handbook qualifications, and the agency keeps their training records for 5 years. The agency keeps each payer's service authorization in the client record. No Medicaid or public-program claim is submitted for a service that was not authorized, not delivered, or not documented.

definitions.definition: Florida's Statewide Medicaid Managed Care Long-Term Care program. AHCA contracts managed care plans that authorize and pay personal care, homemaker, companion and respite services for enrolled members.
The Agency for Persons with Disabilities waiver program under which enrolled individuals receive Personal Supports and other services within an individual budget.
A regional agency under the Department of Elder Affairs that manages the SMMC LTC wait list and contracts home care vendors for elder programs.
A payer's written or electronic approval of the type, amount, frequency and dates of services the agency may deliver and bill for a specific client.
An electronic system that verifies the type of service, the client, the caregiver, the date, the location, and the start and end times of each visit.
The process by which a plan or program reviews and approves a provider to join its network or vendor list.

procedures: The administrator decides, with the governing body, which payers the agency will serve and records the decision in the governing body minutes (GOV-01).
Before accepting any Medicaid-paid client, the administrator enrolls the agency as a Florida Medicaid provider and keeps proof of enrollment in the agency compliance file.

The administrator then applies for credentialing with each SMMC LTC plan operating in the agency's service region. The agency does not accept referrals from a plan until the plan confirms credentialing in writing.
For APD iBudget services, the administrator completes APD provider enrollment for Personal Supports and keeps the approval and the current APD rate documentation on file.
For AAA-funded programs, the administrator completes the AAA's vendor application and contract process and keeps a copy of each executed contract.

On referral, intake staff record the payer, the care or support coordinator's name and phone number, and the authorized service, units and dates. Intake staff verify the authorization directly with the payer before the first visit (SVC-03).

Intake staff screen every assigned caregiver against the payer's qualifications. For iBudget Personal Supports, the caregiver must be at least 18, hold a high school diploma or GED, and have 1 year of verifiable experience (or 30 college semester hours). The administrator places the proof in the personnel file (PER-07).

The RN supervisor and intake staff develop the service plan to match the payer's authorized services and the client's person-centered goals and preferences, and confirm the plan stays within the authorization (SVC-04).

Scheduling staff schedule only authorized services, in the authorized amounts. Aides and personal supports staff may not add, extend or change services without the RN supervisor's approval and a payer authorization change (SVC-09).

Every Medicaid-paid visit is recorded in the EVV system required by the payer. Scheduling staff review EVV exceptions (missed clock-ins, location mismatches, manual edits) each business day and correct them with documented reasons (SVC-10).

Billing staff submit claims only for authorized and verified visits, using the payer's billing codes and negotiated or published rates. Billing staff reconcile claims to EVV records and service notes before submission (GOV-08).

The agency does not bill a client or the client's family for any difference from a Medicaid rate, except where the payer's rules expressly allow it. It also does not bill two payers for the same service hour (CR-07).

The RN supervisor notifies the care or support coordinator within one business day of a significant change in the client's condition, hospitalization, missed visits, safety concern or request to change services. The coordinator's name, the date and the response are recorded (SVC-11).

Intake staff track authorization end dates and request reauthorization or an extension at least 14 days before expiration. Services beyond an expired authorization are not delivered unless the payer has approved them in writing.
The administrator keeps iBudget Personal Supports training records for 5 years and ensures required handbook training is completed and documented.

When a payer denies, reduces or ends services, the RN supervisor tells the client or representative the same day, explains how to appeal through the payer, and starts the transfer or discharge process if needed (SVC-12).

The administrator reviews each payer contract, handbook and rate update when issued, updates this policy and affected forms, and trains staff on changes within 30 days. The date is recorded in the policy review log (GOV-06).
The administrator reports any suspected billing error or overpayment to the payer within the time required by the payer contract and records the correction (GOV-08).

responsibilities.duty: Maintains Medicaid, plan, APD and AAA enrollment and credentialing; signs payer contracts; ensures compliance with payer rules; reviews payer updates.
Verifies authorizations, schedules only authorized services, monitors EVV exceptions, and tracks authorization end dates.
Aligns the service plan with the authorization, communicates changes in condition to care or support coordinators, and supervises caregivers.
Submits only authorized, verified claims and reconciles billing to EVV and service notes.

responsibilities.role: Home Health Aides, CNAs and Personal Supports Staff
responsibilities.duty: Deliver only authorized services, complete EVV for every visit, and report requests for additional services to the RN supervisor.

documentation: Florida Medicaid provider enrollment confirmation
SMMC LTC plan credentialing confirmations and contracts
APD provider enrollment and AAA vendor contracts
Payer service authorizations in each client record, with reauthorization requests
Coordinator communication log
EVV records and exception corrections
iBudget Personal Supports qualification proof and training records (retained 5 years)
Claims and reconciliation records
Policy review log

policies.title: Skilled Services Not Provided — Requirements That Apply If Skilled Services or LPNs Are Added
policies.applies_to: Governing body, administrator, alternate administrator, RN supervisor and, if hired, the director of nursing and LPNs
policies.purpose: To state clearly that [AGENCY NAME] is licensed for non-skilled services only, and to set out in advance the requirements and policies that will apply before any skilled service or LPN is added.
